case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 02.12.2008, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 6254 of 2008 (analogous Judgment with Writ Petition No. 7346 of 2007)
full_judgment:
B.K. Das J.:- This petition for leave to appeal has arisen against the judgment and order dated 2.12.2008 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 6254 of 2008 (Analogously heard with Writ Petition No. 7346 of 2007 and disposed of by a common judgment) disposing of the writ petition directing Artha Rin Adalat No. 3 Dhaka to dispose of Money Execution Case No. 51 of 1992 filed by the decree-holder after deduction of the decreetal amount payable to the decree-holder Bank from the decreetal amount payable by the decree-holder Bank in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 pending before the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka and also directed the Joint District Judge 3rd Court., Dhaka to start execution proceeding in Money Execution Case No. 03 of 1999 for realization of the decreetal amount which would remain after deduction of the decreetal amount payable to the decree-holder Bank. 

2. Sufia Re-Rolling and Steel Mills Ltd. through its Managing Director and 5 other directors have filed Writ Petition No. 7346 of 2007 against Bank of Credit & Commerce at present Eastern. Bank Ltd. Head office and its managing Director challenging an auction notice published in daily newspaper in Money Execution Case No. 51 of 1992 of Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka while the Eastern Bank Ltd. has filed writ Petition No. 6254 of 2008 against the aforesaid Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. and its managing director and other directors challenging the part of the decree passed on 17.1.1991 in Title Suit No. 219 of 1.987 of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.1, Dhaka and also the order dated 11.5.2008 passed in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 of the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka. The said Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 against Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. and its directors for realiyation of loan and that suit was ultimately decreed for an amount of Tk. 75,06,904.69 with interest at the rate of 18% from the date of filing of the suit till the date of passing of the decree. During continuation of that Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. and its directors filed Money Suit No.  47 of 1991 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against the Bank of Credit & Commerce (now Eastern Bank Ltd.) for realization of Tk.68,6995851/21. Title Suit No. 47 of 1991 was decreed on 11.1.1999 for an amount of Tk. 2,85,24,630.21 with interest at the rate of 18% till realization of the decreetal amount. Against the said decree the judgment debtor bank filed E No.108 of 1999 in the High Court Division which was allowed in part on 31.8.2004 and the decreetal amount was reduced to taka 43,22,114.21 with interest at the rate of 18% from the date of filing of the suit till realization. The plaintiff Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. and others then filed Civil petition for leave to appeal No. 1556 of 2004 before the Appellate Division against the judgment passed in EA. No. 108 of 1999 but the said leave petition was dismissed on 5.8.2007. The decree-holder plaintiff Bank of Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 filed Title Execution Case No. 51 of 1992 for realization of the decretal amount and in that title execution case notice for auction of the mortgaged property was published on 10.8.2007 and at that stage the judgment-debtor Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. and others filed Writ Petition No. 7346 of 2007 before the High Court Division and obtained rule and also an order of stay of further proceeding of Title Execution Case No. 51 of 1992. Sufia Re-Roiling and still Mills Ltd. and its Directors, who are the decree-holders in Money Suit No. 47 of 1991, filed Execution Case being Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 in the 3rd Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for realisation of the decreetal amount along with interest who rejected the claim for set off by the impugned order dated 11.5.2008 holding that since both the execution cases were pending in two different courts, set off was not possible. Thereafter on 18.8.2008 the decree holder bank filed Writ Petition No. 6254 of 2008 challenging the decree dated 17.1.1991 passed in Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 exonerating the defendants from paying the interest till the date of realization of decreetal amount and also the order dated 11.5.2008 passed in Money Execution Cases No. 3 of 1999 rejecting the bank's application for set off. Rule was issued in this Writ Petition on 18.8.2008 and on that date an order also was passed staying all further proceedings of Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1999. 

3. The learned Judges of the High Court Division noticed "From the above stated admitted facts it is evident that both the sets of Writ Petitioners have got one decree for money each against the other. Admittedly the Writ Petitioner Eastern Bank Limited has got a decree for an amount of TK. 75,00,904/- with interest at the rate of Tk.18% from the date of filing of the suit till the date of passing of the decree. The borrower Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. also admittedly has .got a decree for Tk. 43, 22,114.21 with interest at the rate of Tk. 18% from the date of filing of the suit till realization of decreetal amount payable to the Writ Petitioners Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. is not fixed rather, it is increasing day by day. And undisputedly the decreetal amount payable to Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. has grown up by this time, much more than the decreetal amount payable to Eastern Bank Limited." The High Court Division further noticed "However, since both the contesting parties before us have got a decree for money against the other party we asked both the parties to make a settlement themselves, but in-spite of taking some time from us for making settlement both of them failed to reach any settlement and they have prayed for an equitable order from this court to settle the matter. We have considered facts and circumstances deeply. The decretal amount payable to the Writ Petitioner Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd. has increased much more than the decreetal amount payable to the Writ Petition Eastern Bank Limited and this amount is increasing day by day. In this circumstances we find it just and proper to deduct the decretal amount payable to the Writ Petitioners Eastern Bank Limited as this amount is increasing day by day. Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 and Title Execution Case No. 51 of 1992 which arc pending Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka should be disposed of on full satisfaction after making necessary note of this fact of deduction of the decreetal amount payable to the decree holder bank from the decreetal amount payable by this decree holder bank in Money Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 pending in Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka. We therefore, be disposed of on full satisfaction after making necessary note of this fact of deduction of the decreetal amount payable to the decree holder Sufia Re-Rolling & Steel Mills Ltd." with the aforesaid observations the Writ Petitions were disposed of by the High Court Division. 

4. We have heard the submissions of the learned Advocates for the petitioners in both the petitions and also respondent in both the petitions and perused the impugned orders and all other materials on record. We have also considered the decree passed in Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 and minutely considered the words used in the decree exonerating defendant No.2 from levying any interest on him till the decree was passed in Title Suit No. 219 of 1987 i.e. 17.1.1991 till the decreetal amount is realized from the date of the judgment dated 17.1.1991. 

5. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case and the terms of the decree we do not find any merit in this leave petition. 

6. Accordingly the leave petition is dismissed. 

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 22.01.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 227 of 2003)
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J:- Instant Retition. under Article 193 of the Constitution is for granting leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 22.01.2009  passed in Civil Revision No. 227 of 2003 by the High Court Division making the Rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 51 of 2002 by the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, restoring the Money Suit No. 11 of 1992 to its original file and number, on an application filed under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

2. The respondent No. 1 hereof as plaintiff filed the Money Suit No. 11 of 1992 claiming Tk. 23,82,111.13/- together with interest @ 18% and cost from the petitioner hereof being defendant in the suit. 

3. The defendant filed written statement to resist the claim of the plaintiff but the suit was allowed to be decreed ex-parte on 03.06.2000 and subsequently on receipt of auction notice from Court, the said defendant filed Miscellaneous Case No. 51 of 2002 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the original Money Suit No. 11 of 1992 after setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 03.06.2000. 

4. The plaintiff of Money Suit as opposite party contested the miscellaneous case by filing written objection and the learned Joint District Judge upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record allowed the petition by order dated 31.10.2002 awarding compensation of Tk.5,000/- in favour of the plaintiff. 

5. Being aggrieved there-against the plaintiff moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 227 of 2003. The Rule was contested by the defendant. The High Court Division on consideration of the materials and evidence on record and the submissions of the learned Advocate of the contesting par-ties made the Rule absolute, observing that: (a) "In course of the hearing of this rule, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has placed before us the entire order sheet of the suit. It appeared from the order sheet that the defendants had full knowledge about the institution of the suit and they filed written statement as back as on 17th August, 1992 and there-after the suit was fixed for peremptory hearing 22nd April 1995. On 16th July, 1995 the plaintiff filed an application for recording his evidence on commission and the prayer was allowed on 22nd July, 1995. The Advocate Commissioner there-upon submitted commission report on 9th September, 1996. Thereafter the defendant filed 2 applications on 12th August, 1996 and 13th August, 1996 for rejection of the Advocate Commissioner's report and to enable them to cross-examine the plaintiff. The learned Subordinate Judge rejected the prayers on 20th May, 1997. The defendants there-upon renewed their prayer for cross-examination of the - plaintiff. The learned Subordinate Judge by order dated 5th August, 1997 allowed the prayer and directed them to file Commission fee of Tk. 1000/- by 4th September, 1997. On the date fixed, the defendants did not file the Commission fee: On the next date on 25th September, 1997 the defendant did not take any step in the matter and the matter was fixed on 18th October, 1997 for submitting commission fee. On 19th October 1997 the defendants did not file the commission fee. The plaintiff filed an application for rejecting the defendants prayer for cross-examination of the plaintiff. The learned Subordinate Judge rejected the application and fixed 13th November, 1997 for depositing commission fee. On the date fixed the defendants did not deposit the commission fee and the learned Subordinate Judge again fixed on 8th January, 1998 for filing com-mission fee. On 8th January, 1998 the defendants did not deposit commission fee and on the next date on 2nd February, 1998 also the defendant did not deposit the commission 
fee. Accordingly the learned Subordinate Judge fixed 8th March, 1998 for peremptory hearing. On that day the defendants did not take any step in the matter and it was adjourned to 12th April, 1998 the suit was ultimately adjourned on many occasions and ultimately it was taken up for ex-parte hearing 15th March, 1999. The learned Subordinate Judge thereupon issued show cause notice upon the defendants as to why the order dated 5th august, 1997 allowing their prayer for cross-examination of the plain-tiff should not be vacated. The defendant’s did not take any step on 31st March, 1999 and 28th April, 1999 and ultimately the suit was decreed ex-parte." and (b) "Admittedly the defendants had knowledge about the pendency of the suit and the recording of the plaintiffs evidence ex-parte. Despite that fact the learned Subordinate Judge afforded the defendants to contest the suit and allowed their prayer to cross examine the plaintiffs witness but they did not deposit the commission fees on 4th September, 1997, 25th September, 1997, 19th October 1997, 13th November, 1997, 8th January, 1998, 2nd February, 1998 and thereafter they did not take any step on 8th March, 1998, 11th April, 1998 and 11th October, 1998. Even after issuance of the show cause notice on 15th March, 1998, they did not take any step in the matter. The learned Joint District Judge himself found the neglect and laches on the part of the defendants in prosecuting the matter. The learned Joint District Judge on perusal of the evidence of P.W. 1 noticed that though the defendants imputed the blame upon their Advocate Manik Mridha but said Manik Mridha remain as panel Advocate for the Chittagong Port Trust and accordingly disbelieved their plea. The learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit after eight years six months of the date of institution. Thereafter they filed for setting aside the exparte decree after One year eleven months eighteen days on 19th June 2002. They did not explain the delay properly. The learned Joint District Judge was not also satisfied with the explanation and even then without condoning the delay allowed the application on flimsy ground." and (c) "As observed above, the suit was instituted in January, 1992 for recovery-of huge amount of money and for years together, the defendants were afforded sufficient opportunity to contest in the suit but they failed to take any step in the matter. The learned Joint District Judge himself found that there was neglect and laches on the part of the defendants in prosecuting the matter. The reason for which the learned Joint District Judge has set aside the ex-parte decree and allowed the Misc. Case is based upon misconception of law. The Court has no power to set aside an ex-parte decree for ends of justice or for any cause other than its satisfaction that the defendant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing. The defendants have miserably failed to satisfy the Court in that regard and accordingly, the learned Joint District Judge arbitrarily set aside the ex-parte decree without being satisfied that the defendants were prevented by sufficient cause when the suit was called on for ex-parte decree. Since the trial Court itself found that there was neglect and laches of the defendants in prosecuting the matter, it ought not have exercised the inherent powers in setting aside the ex-parte decree overriding the express provisions that there must be sufficient ground for believing that the defendants were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing. The learned Joint District Judge in the premises arbitrarily exercised its discretion in setting aside the ex-parte decree which is required to be interfered with." 

6. We have perused the leave petition, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division and of the Court below and considered the submissions made by the learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner. 

7. The learned Advocate found it difficult to overcome the laches on the part of the petitioner in proceeding with the case. The learned Advocate however tried to put blame on the learned Advocate of the petitioner, who con-ducted the suit in the trial Court. 

8. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case as disclosed in the observations made by the High Court Division, quoted hereinabove, we are of the view that the default was made by the petitioner in contesting suit. The premium given by the trial Court, in restoring the suit to its file and number in-spite of the gross negligence found on the part of the petitioner hereof in con-ducting the case cannot be sustained. We find that the decision arrived at by the High Court Division is an 'accordance with law and no interference is called for. 

9. The petition is accordingly dismissed.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 20th day of February, 2007 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2150 of 2001)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. This appeal, by leave, is from the judgment and order the 20th day of February, 2007 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2150 of 2011 making the Rule absolute.

<u>2. Facts necessary for disposal of this petition are that respondent No. 1 as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 30 of 1998 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Lakhai, Habiganj for permanent injunction stating, inter alia, that the suit land belonged to Sharifun Nessa Chowdhury, proforma respondent No. 5 (as stated in the plaint, hereinafter referred to as defendant No.5). Defendant No. 5 acquired title to the suit land and secured her possession therein through amicable partition amongst her co-sharers and her name was correctly recorded in the last settlement survey, but in some portion of the suit land, being patit, the villagers of Shingana-village used to graze cattle since the time immemorial. The villagers requested defendant No. 5 to make waqf of the said land to increase the income of the village mosque to which she agreed and then she, by an unregistered waqf deed dated 08.03.1960, made waqf of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff mosque. The Mutwalli of the waqf, at a huge cost of the waqf, reclaimed the suit land and grew crops therein for the last 15 years, but as some complications arose in the absence of a registered deed, defendant No. 5, by a registered waqf deed dated 8th of Bhadra, 1405 B.S transferred the suit land to the plaintiff mosque and the plaintiff mosque continued its possession and managed its property through a Managing Committee of which the Mutawalli was the president. The musallis of the mosque collectively leased out the suit land on cash basis to different persons and with the money so raised, the salaries of the Imam and the Moazzin are being paid and other development works of the mosque are also done. Defendant No. 1 had no title or possession in the suit land, but due to some misunderstanding with him over the formation of the Masjid Committee, he and his relations, defendant Nos.2-4, had been trying to create disturbances with regard to possession of the suit land and hence the plaintiff mosque filed the suit.</u>

3. The suit was contested by defendant No. I (hereinafter referred to as the defendant) appellant herein, by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that defendant No. 5 by a registered deed dated 11.07.1975, earlier sold 186 acres land out of suit Plot No. 500 to Imam Baksh and 13 others and one Moazzen Hussain Chowdhury also sold some land from the said plot to said Imam Baksh and 30 others by a kabala dated 30.12.1974, Imam Baksh having acquired title and possession in respect of 48 acre land out of the scheduled land sold the same to the defendant by a registered kabla dated 15.03.1998 who, on getting possession thereof, cultivated IRRI crops therein. In an earlier suit being Title Suit No. 356 of 1984 of the Court of Munsif, Lakhai filed by Imam Baksh, it was decided that defendant No. 5 and Moazzen Hossain Chowdhury had no title in the remaining portion of the land of Plot No. 500 and defendant Nos. 1-37 of that suit acquired no title in the said plot and as such, when defendant No. 5 executed and registered the disputed waqf deed, she had no subsisting title in the land transferred, so the plaintiff mosque did not acquire any title in the suit land by virtue of the deed of transfer made on 8th Bhadra, 1405 B.S. Moreover '05 acre land of Plot No. 499 and '53 acre land of Plot No. 891 belonged to Jalaluddin Chowdhury and he being in possession thereof as the rightful owner sold the same to the defendant by a registered deed of sale dated 14.10.1996 and he has been in possession thereof by rearing fishes therein and as such, the plaintiff was not entitled to get any decree in the suit and the same was liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 12.08.1999 decreed the suit.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the defendant preferred Title Appeal No. 129 of 1999 before the District Judge, Habiganj. The learned Subordinate Judge, second court, Habiganj hearing the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 28.03.2001 allowed the appeal, set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and dismissed the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the Appellate court, the plaintiff mosque filed Civil Revision No. 2150 of 2001 before the High court Division and obtained the Rule. A learned Judge of the Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute, set aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate court and restored those of the trial court. Having felt aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendant filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1050 of 2007 before this court and leave was granted on 15.10.2008 to consider the submissions made by the teamed Advocate for the appellant as under:

"The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge found that " বাদীর উচিৎ ছিল নালিশী ৫০০ নং দাগের তাহার দাবীকৃত ১.৮৫ ভূমির ও নালিশা ৪৯৯ নং দাগের তাহার দাবীকৃত ৪৩(sic) একর ভূমির সুস্পষ্ট চৌহুদ্দি পৃথক ভাবে উল্লেখ করা। এই সংগত কারনে বাদী তাহার দাবীকৃত নাঃ  ভূমির চৌহুদ্দি তফসিলে স্পষ্ট ভাবে উল্লেখ করিতে ব্যর্থ হিইয়াছেন। … নথি দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় বাদী তাহার দখলের সমর্থনে সাক্ষীদের দ্বারা কোন খাজনার দাখিলা প্রমান করেন নাই বা এ ব্যাপারে যুক্তি সংগত কোন বক্তব্য দেন নাই। …. বাদী পক্ষ সুস্পষ্ট ভাবে নালিশের ভূমিতে চৌহুদ্দি চিহ্নিত করিতে ব্যর্থ হইয়াছে।…. ইহা স্পষ্ট ভাবে প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, বিরোধী ভূমিতে বাদী/রেসপনডেন্ট এর কোন দখর প্রমাণিত হয় নাই। " and accordingly the High Court Division ought to have discharged the Rule but instead the High Court Division without adverting the above findings made the Rule absolute."

6. Mrs. Sufia Khatun, learned Advocate-on-Record, for the appellant has submitted that the Appellate court rightly dismissed the suit inasmuch as the plaintiff failed to specify the suit land as required under Order VII, rule 3 of the code of the Civil Procedure and also failed to prove its exclusive possession in the suit land, the High Court Division erred in law in interfering with the judgment and decree of the Appellate court and as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside and the appeal be allowed.

7. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent, on the other hand, has submitted that the plaintiff mosque proved its exclusive possession in the suit land, which has been rightly found by the trial court, but the Appellate court though the last court of fact did not reverse the said finding of the trial court with reference to the evidence on record and on an erroneous view that the suit land was not specifically butted and bounded by the boundary dismissed the suit. Mr. Bhuiyan has submitted that besides the oral evidence that the plaintiff mosque is in possession of the suit land, the suit land was recorded in the khatian in the name of plaintiff mosque. He has further submitted that the mosque could not pay the rent earlier due to the Governments decision exempting the mosque from paying rent, but after withdrawal of the Government's decision, now the mosque is paying rent in respect of the suit land. Therefore, the High Court Division did not commit any error of law in setting aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court and restoring those of the trial court and as such, there is no merit in the appeal and the same is liable to be dismissed.

8. From the leave granting order, it is clear that leave was granted to consider the submissions made on behalf of the appellant that the High court Division was not justified   in restoring those of the trial court decreeing the suit in view of the finding of the Appellate court that the plaintiff failed to describe the suit land with specification and that the plaintiff in support of its claim of possession in the suit land failed to prove any rent receipt through any of its witnesses.

9. Let us see first whether the Appellate court was correct in giving the finding as to the vagueness or un-specification of the suit land. In the concise statement, it has been specifically stated that in the written statement, the defendant did not raise any objection as to the un-specification or vagueness of the suit land. From the judgment of the trial court, it does not also appear that any objection was raised as to the vagueness or un-specification of the suit land and no issue in that regard was framed as well by the trial court, so we find the statements made in the concise statement correct. Plaint of the suit has not been filed with the paper book, but the decree of the trial court has been filed. From the decree, it appears that the suit land has been clearly identified by the chauhaddis. Therefore, we find no vagueness or un-specification in the suit land.

<u>10. It is a well settled principle of law that in a suit for permanent injunction, the prime consideration is whether the plaintiff is in exclusive possession of the suit land. It is also a settled principle of law that title can be gone into incidentally. From the judgment and decree of the trial court, it appears that it considered the evidence on record and gave clear finding that the plaintiffs witnesses proved its possession in the suit land. The trial Court also found prima facie title of the plaintiff in the suit land. From the judgment of the Appellate Court, it appears that it itself noted that the plaintiffs witnesses, namely; PWs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 deposed that the plaintiff mosque is in the possession of the suit land and the defendants by cross-examining them could not extract anything in their favour. In the concise statement, it has been stated that the name of the plaintiff mosque has been recorded in the recent survey and also in the field survey and no objection was raised by the defendant under rules 30 and 31 of the Tenancy Rules. In the concise statement, it has been further stated that in the revisional survey, the lands of two plots involved in the suit being plot Nos. 499 and 500, were recorded in the name of the plaintiff mosque in new Plot Nos. 780 and 819 respectively appertaining to new khatian being No. 350 and rent has been paid by the Mutualli under the new khatian which were filed before the High Court Division which conclusively proved that the plaintiff mosque is in possession in the suit land.</u>

<u>11. Mrs. Sufia Khatun could not dispute the assertion made in the concise statement that the suit land has been separately recorded in the two new plots mentioned above and a new khatian has been opened in the name of the plaintiff mosque. The very recording of the land of the suit plots in separate khatian in the name of the mosque and subsequent payment of rent prima facie proved that the plaintiff is in exclusive possession of the specified area of the suit land and the plaintiffs witnesses also clearly proved its possession in the suit land. Even if it is accepted that the plaintiff did not file any rent receipt showing payment of rent at the earliest point of time that could not nullify the oral evidence of the PWs that the plaintiff was in possession in the suit land.</u>

12. For the discussions made above, we find nothing wrong with the impugned judgment and order and no merit in the appeal.

13. Accordingly, this appeal is dismissed. There will be no order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Sharif Uddin Chaklader, ,J: This Rule under Section 5 read with Section 14 of the Limitation Act, 1908 for condonation of delay of 814 days for filing Miscellaneous Appeal under Order XLIII Rule 1(h)(iii) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 against Order No.49 dated 15.6.2009 passed by the learned Judge of Arthawrin Adalat, 1st Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No.25 of 2009 arising out of Artha Execution Case No.189 of 2005 arising from exparte judgment and decree dated 8.9.2004 passed in Arthawrin Case No:623 of 2004 rejecting the application filed under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The aforesaid suit was filed against Towhidul Islam, Towfiqul Islam, Rownak Jaml, Selina Mohid, all sons and daughters of late Azizul Islam, for realization of Tk.70,70,436.28/- arising out of loan obtained by the said defendants vide sanction letter No. T.C.R/Songgri:Ni:Ri:/ Monowara-834 dated 9.10.93 and also vide sanction letter No.Pro:Ka:/Sagriribi-3/433 1 dated 21.1 1.94 of Tk.19,00,000.00 for the purpose of constructing building. Schedule of the property mortgaged in deed Nos.4509/4510 dated 25.10.1993 and Ammoktar Nama deed Nos.5258, 5259 dated 26.11.94 described in Kha scheduled of the aforesaid suit is as follows: 

“সম্পত্তির তফসিল-খ
জেলা-ঢাকা, থানা-রমনা, হালে মতিঝিল, মৌজা-রমনা, খতিয়ান নং-সি.এস.১০৪, এস, এ ৩৩৯, আর, এস, ১২০৯ মিউট্রেশন খতিয়ান নং-৩৩৯/১, প্লট নং সি, এস, ১৫০ এস, এ, ১৯৬৮ আর, এস, ২৮8২, জমির পরিমান .০8৫০ অযুতাংশ ও তদন্থিত নির্মিত ইমারত স্ট্রাকচার, ফিকচার, ফিটিংস, বাউন্ডারী ওয়াল সহ যাহার মিউনিসিপ্যাল হোল্ডিং নং-৫৮/১-এ পুরানা পল্টন ঢাকা। যাহার চৌহদ্দি: উত্তরে রাস্তা , দক্ষিনে: রাস্তা, পূর্বে হোল্ডিং নং ৫৯, পশ্চিমে ৫৮/১ –এ, কচি কাচার মেলার অফিস , পুরানা পল্টন, ঢাকা। 
After completion of clue process of law suit was filed and after filing of the suit, on 18.8.2004 plaintiff filed application for amendment of schedule of the mortgaged land as follows: 

“প্রস্তাবিত সংশোধনী
আর্জির ‘খ’ নং তফছিলের যেখানে প্লট নং-সি,এস, “১৫ ০" লিপি আছে ঊহা কর্তন হইয়া তদস্থলে “১৫৫" হইবে এবং একইভাবে মর্টগেজ দলিলের যে স্থানে “১৫o" সি,এস, দাগ লিপি আছে উহা কর্তন হইয়া তদস্থলে “১৫৫" অংক লিপি হইবে ৷”
2, This amendment in fact attracts the land of the 3rd party appellant-petitioner. Learned Judge of Arthawrin Adalat on the next date i.e. one day after on 19.8.2004 decreed the suit. Thereafter, decree holder bank put the decree into execution in Execution Case No.1,89 of 2005 on 23.2.2005 against the amendment mortgaged land which includes 3rd party appellant land i.e. C.S. Plot No.155. Petitioner having came to know of the aforesaid execution case rushed to the Court filed application under Order 1 Rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil' Procedure read with section 57 of the Arthawrin Adalat Ain, 2003 on 12.10.2005 for adding him as party to put forward his case in respect of C.S. Plot No.155. Said application was rejected. Thereafter, the petitioner through his constituted Power of Attorney holder filed Writ Petition No.8021 of 2005 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule and also order of stay of the proceeding of Artha Zari Case No.189 of 2005. Ultimately Rule was discharged.  Against which 3rd party petitioner filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1329 of 2008 and on the advice of the lawyer's petitioner did not press the said petition. It was further advised to file application under the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure before the civil Court. Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal, was dismissed as being not .pressed on 6.4.2009. 

3. It is the case of the petitioner that the heirs of Nawab Ali Yearor Khan i.e. 3rd party petitioner neither mortgaged their property to the opposite party bank nor stood as guarantor of the loan availed by the defendants to, the Arthawrin Suit. The auction, notice is illegal and void for which petitioner submitted application under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure for getting schedule property released from attachment but the learned Judge of Arthawrin Adalat reject the same holding that 10% decretal amount would he deposited which have not been deposited. 

4. Mr. S. N. Goswami learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, submits that, learned Judge of the Arthawrin Adalat committed -gross illegality in not treating the application filed by the appellant under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure but under provision of Arthawrin  Ain. Learned Advocate further submits that 3rd party appellant-petitioner 'wants that court should hold an investigation before hanging 3rd party appellant-petitioner from losing his property of Plot No.155, 

5. Learned Advocate relied on the case of Moshammat Sufia Begum and Others Vs. Sonali Bank Ltd. reported in 16 Bur. 300 wherein a Division Bench of this Court held that 

"10. 0n perusal of impugned order it appears that the learned executive Court without carrying  on any investigation into the payer has rejected the said application only on the reason that the present petitioners are sons, daughter and wife of the judgment debtor Abdul Mannan. It appears that in the application made under Order 21 Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure the petitioners have specifically asserted that the schedule land has been transferred by a deed of gift dated 12.11.1997 and the Money Suit was instituted by the decree holder On 6.10.1998. It further appears that the present petitioners submitted the said deed of gift before the Executing Court along with a prayer for getting released the land from attachment. The law provides that where any claim is preferred to. or any objection is made to the attachment of ally property attached in execution of a decree on the ground that such property is not liable to such attachment, the Court, shall proceed to investigate the claim or objection with the like power as regards the examination of the claimant or objector, and in all other respects, as if he was a  party to the suit. (Underlining made by us) This provision imposes duty upon the Executing Court for holding a true investigation mandatory but in the instant case without executing any investigation the Court has rejected the application of the present petitioner summarily by a non speaking order. In view of the non speaking order and, that the impugned order having passed without having any investigation, we are of the view that impugned order has been passed not in accordance with the provision of Order 21 Rule 58 of the Code of CM1 Procedure. By the impugned order the Court below has committed an error of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice." 

6. Mrs. Hosne Ara Begum, learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiff-decree holder-respondent-opposite party, on the other hand submits that, if any decree passed against 3rd party, 3rd party is not remedy less as Section 32 of the Arthawrin Adalat Ain, 2003 provided remedy for the 3rd party which provides that 10% decretal amount ought to be deposited. 

7. Learned Advocate relied on the case of Peninsular Shipping Service Ltd. Vs. Faruque Paint and Vanish Manufacturing Co. Ltd. and others. 59 DLR (AD)-26. Learned Advocate also relied on Section 41(1)(2) of the Arthawrin Adalat Act. Appellate Division held that: 

"filing of appeal under Sub-section (1) is subject to fulfillment of the requirement of Sub-section (2) of the Ain and both the provisions are conjunctive and not disjunctive and the law being a special law there is no way out to escape the limitation." 

8. Learned Advocate also relied on an unreported decision of the Appellate Division passed on 25.8.2011 in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1700 of 2009 which was arising out of an order passed by this Court in Civil Order No.2760 of 2009 summarily rejected the application filed under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure in between the same parties. Wherein it is held that security money is required to be deposited. Appellate Division held as: 

"Petitioner's application under Order 21, Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure was passed in accordance with Section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain; 2003. The contention of this petitioner's learned Counsel that the Artha Rin Adalat passed the said order under Order 21, Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not correct at all. The application under Order 21, Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed as per provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and the rejection of the same also was ordered in accordance with the provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003." 

9. The question calls for determination in the instant case is that whether Arthawrin Adalat was legal and justified in decreeing the suit in respect of land of petitioner of C.S. Plot No.155 which was included in the suit just one day before the decree.  
10. It is admitted position that when the suit proceeds the property of the petitioner of Plot No.155 was included and it was include by amendment just one day before pronouncement of judgment on exparte. It may be true, the suit was .proceeding with 1-41 wrong schedule of the .property mortgaged, and that may be mistake and when the mistake detected it may be corrected but before passing the judgment, learned Judge ought to give notice to the holder of the property i.e. in title holder of the case property. It may be it has no Connection with the original loanee or he is not relating to the suit property but in such situation, justice demand notice ought to be sent.to the person who has title over the suit plot, that has not been done goes to show that fraud has been practiced in including the property of the b°- petitioner-appellant. When fraud has been detected as decree holder surreptitiously includes the property in the decree, appellant has a right to agitate his grievance before the appellate forum. 

11. Second question-as crept is that whether an investigation is required when 3I'd party challenged the decree on the ground of fraud. It has been settled all through that if 3rd party filed 'application under Order XXI Rule 58 of the. Code of Civil Procedure invoking the provision of the Code of Civil Procedure in getting redress for protecting the property, it is to be filed before the Arthawrin. Adalat, not before the civil Court as decree has been passed by Arthawrin Adalat. But application under- Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure upon which the miscellaneous case proceed which cannot he done or file as per provision of Arthawrin Adalat Ain as Ain made restricted application of Code of Civil Procedure. This proceeding although before the ArthaWrin Adalat but independent of the proceeding of Arthawrin Ain but order is to he passed by Arthawrin Adalat as the decree passed by the Adalat and since the proceeding arisen out of an application filed under provision of Code of Civil Procedure, in such position. this order cannot be said to be passed as per provision of Arthawrin Ain but as per provision of Code of Civil Procedure. On these facts Section. 43 of the Arthawrin Adalat Ain cannot be invoked as it requires deposition of 10% decretal amount which is mandatory. Section 43 of the Ain relates to the parties who are before the Court or Adalat. Appellant has been brought in court by the decree holder by amending the schedule of the application just One day before the exparte decree was passed without notifying the appellant. Section 43 of the Ain although give a right to appeal but with a penalty clause of depositing 10% of the decretal amount. The person having no knowledge of the proceeding and his property has been included in the schedule just one day before the decree, in such position. Appellant shall not he required to pay 10% decretal amount. 

12. From the fact it is clear that fraud has been practiced in getting exparte decree as such we are of the view that delay as has been occurred in preferring the appeal, as of right of the appellant-petitioner, is to be condoned.
 
13. Another things is that provision of Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure is mandatory. Law required an investigation but impugned order as passed was passed treating the application as per provision of Arthawrin Ain which is totally illegal. 

14. It appears that Arthawrin Ain promulgated for realizing Loan money given by different institution but we see that innocent people has been harassing as such the law should be re-consider by the law makers so that 3Id party should not be harassed in this manner. 

15. In the result, this rule i.e. Civil Rule No.880(fm) of 2011 is made absolute. 

16. The delay of 814 days in filing the appeal is condoned. 

17. Office is directed to place first miscellaneous appeal before the appropriate Bench immediately for admission. 

18. A copy of the judgment be sent to the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, the People's Republic of Bangladesh immediately. 

19. Communicate this order at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. A.N.M. Bashir Ullah, J :- This Rule, on an application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the CPC) at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show as to why the judgment and decree dated 25.04.2006 passed by the Joint District Judge, Court, Noakhali, in Other Appeal No.17 of 1992 reversing those dated 30.09.1991 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Noakhali in Title Suit No.274 of 1988 should not be set aside and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that Md. Belayet Hossain, 
the predecessor of the petitioners as plaintiff filed the above numbered suit for 
declaration of his title into .38 acres of land described in the schedule `ga' of the plaint contending inter-alia that 2.70 acres of land appertaining to CS Khatian No.6 of Purbo Mohodari mouja under Noakhali Sadar Police Station originally belonged to Tuka Mia and the said land was recorded correctly in his name. 

3. Tuka Mia died leaving behind 3 sons Kobbat Mia, Abdul Gafur and-Kala Mia and one daughter Badrun Nesa. The heirs of Tuka Mia jointly sold 1.18 acres of land by a registered kabala dated 18.1.1968 to Azizul Hoq. While Azizul Hoq was in possession of the said land sold the same to the late plaintiff Md. Belayet Hossain by a registered kabala dated 19.4.1969. Out of the said 1.18 acres of land .88 acres of land has been correctly recovered in the name of Kobbat Mia and others in Plot No.531 at Ayubpur mouja but the remaining .38 acres of land has been wrongly recorded in plot No.40 in Khatian No.1 in the name of the Government but there was no reason for such recording. The plaintiff had no knowledge about the said wrong record of right but on 02.8.1988 the plaintiff came to know about the said wrong record of right, hence the suit. 

4. During the pendency of the suit the original plaintiff Md. Belayet Hossain died, as such, his heirs the present-petitioners were substituted as plaintiffs in the suit on 06.2.1989. 

5. The suit was contested by the defendant No.1 filing written statement. In the written statement it was averred that the suit was not maintainable, the suit is hit under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the plaintiff had filed a test suit having no real cause of action. The case of the defendant No.1, in short, is that before the CS record of right the suit land had gone into the water of the river and after 20 years the land was reformed-in-situ and as such under the provision of P.0.15 of 1972 and also under Section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the suit land has been vested to the government as khas land. The plaintiff has no right, title and interest into the suit land and the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

6. Upon the above pleadings, the trial Court framed as many as 5 issues to dispose of the suit. The plaintiffs examined 2 witnesses and filed some documentary evidences which were marked as exhibit Nos.l-3 but the contesting defendant neither examined any witness nor filed any documentary evidence to prove his case. The trial Court upon consideration of evidence on record decreed the suit declaring the title of the plaintiffs into the suit land by his judgment dated 30.9.1991. 

7. The defendant No.1 against the said judgment of the trial Court preferred Title Appeal No.17 of 1992 in the Court of District Judge, Noakhali which has been ultimately heard by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Noakhali. During the pendency of the appeal in the appellate Court below one Mozibul Hoq son of Soleman was added as respondent No.2 in the appeal who filing a written statement in the appellate Court below averred that Tuka Mia while was -exercising his right, title and possession into 2.70 acres of land, the land was sold in auction and Sree Prosanna Kumar Das had purchased the land and the said sale was confirmed on 15.11.1924 and in the M.R. record of right the land was correctly recorded in his name in Khatian No.6 and 9. In the Diara settlement 2.24 acres of land out of the said 2.70 acres of land was wrongly recorded in the name of Kobbat Mia and others, the heirs of Tuka Mia. The remaining .46 acres of land was wrongly recorded in Plot No.40 in Khatian No.1 in the name of the government. 

8. After the death of Prosanna Kumar Das his daughter's son Sree Sudhir Ranjan Bosu inherited the land from Prosanna Kumar Das. Sree Sudhir Ranjan Bosu sold 1.09 acres of land to Amena Khatun, the mother of added respondent Mozibul Hoq. Thereafter Amena Khatun gifted the said land to his son Mozibul Hoq by a deed of heba on 14.12.1986. Amena Khatun filed Title Suit No.161 of 1983 for declaration of her title into the suit land as some portion of her land was recorded in the name of Government. The said suit was decreed but in the appeal the said suit was sent back on remand and as such the said suit was renumbered as 163 of 2004 and is pending in the Court of Assistant Judge, Chatkhil for disposal and in the said suit the Md. Belayet Hossain, the predecessor of the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.274 of 1988 was a defendant. 

9. The appellate Court below considering the case of the added respondent Mozibul Hoq opined that since added respondent Mozibul Hoq has been claiming the suit land through auction purchase and since a suit is pending filed by Mozibul Hoq between the same parties for the same land so, the Title Suit No.274 of 1988 should be decided in presence of said Mozibul Hoq and the appellate Court below in fact giving a chance to the plaintiff-petitioners sent the suit back on remand for trial afresh. The plaintiff-petitioners being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree of the appellate Court below dated 25.4.2006 moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

10. Mr. Khair Ezaz Masud, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners supports the Rule. He submits that it is fact that the added respondent Mozibul Hoq appearing in the appeal has been claiming the suit land relying on the auction purchase of Prosanna Kumar Das but the trial Court found the title of the plaintiff into the suit land and the said findings of the trial Court has not been reversed by the appellate Court below. If the suit is sent back on remand to the trial Court for trial afresh the findings and observation of the trial Court below in respect of title of the plaintiff-petitioners should be protected. 

11. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Osman.Gani Khan, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the defendant-opposite party No.1 opposes the Rule. He submits that the suit land has been recorded in Plot No.40 in Khatian No.1 in the name of the Government. Both the plaintiff of the present suit and the added respondent No.2 Mozibul Hoq of the appeal have been claiming the suit land and apart from the present suit there appears another suit pending in the Court below filed by Mozibul Hoq for the same land. So, for proper adjudication and also for an effective and complete justice both the suits should be heard analogously by the trial Court. He also submits that the appellate Court below in order to render equal justice to all the parties had sent the suit back on remand which does not call for any interference from this Court. 

12. I have considered above submissions of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record. 

13. On going to the materials on record it appears that initially the plaintiff had come in the trial Court with a very simple case that he purchased the suit land from Azizul Hoq and Azizul Hoq got the suit land from the heirs of recorded tenant Tuka Mia but in the Diara settlement .38 acres of land has been wrongly recorded in the name of the Government in Plot No.40 in Khatian No.1. 

14. The suit was contested by the Government and Government filed a written statement and in the said written statement it has been asserted that the land had gone into the water and almost after 20 years the land was reformed in situ and by the operation of the law the land had vested to the Government. The case of the Government appears to be very much appetizing to hear but it is surprising to note here that the Government could not even state the name of the river where the land had allegedly drowned into the water. So how can the Government make his case believable that the land is the alluvial land? However, be that as it may the total scenario of the suit has been changed when the added respondent No.2 Mozibul Hoq made his appearance in the scene. 

15. Mozibul Hoq though admitted that the suit land originally belonged to Tuka Mia but his further case is that the land has been sold in an auction and one Prosanna Kumar Das purchased the suit land in the said auction and pursuant to the said purchase in auction the M.R. Khatian was also prepared in the name of Prosanna Kumar Das but in the Diara settlement 2.24 acres of land has been wrongly recorded in the name of the heirs of Tuka Mia and remaining .46 acres of land has been wrongly recorded in the name of the Government and Mozibul Hoq filed a suit for declaration of his title into the said land which is still pending in the competent Court for disposal. 

From the case of the added respondent Mozibul Hoq and the plaint case it appears that both of them targeting the suit land are at logger heads filing two separate suits. 

16. Now, at this stage of the suit I find that in getting a declaration as to the title of the plaintiffs into the suit land the Government's stand is not the main hindrance for the plaintiffs in the present suit rather the plaintiffs are to cross the hurdle imposed by added respondent Mozibul Hoq and this findings are also applicable vice versa for Mozibul Hoq. 

Thus the appellate Court below rightly held that the plaintiff can be granted relief only in presence of Mozibul Hoq. In my consideration the appellate Court below for an effective and complete justice has given the equal chance to both the plaintiff and Mozibul Hoq sending the suit back on remand. I find no error of law or illegality in the findings and decisions of the appellate Court below rather in my consideration sending the suit back on remand he has done an equal justice to both the parties. 

17. From the materials on record it is further found that both the plaintiff and added respondent have been litigating for the same land through two separate suits. So to avoid conflicting decision of the suits, both the suits should be tried analogously. In fact for an effective and complete justice also it would be wiser if both the suit file by the plaintiff and added respondent Mozibul Hoq are heard analogously by the Court below. 

18. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The trial Court is directed to dispose of the Title Suit No.274 of 1988 filed by the plaintiff-petitioners of this Rule and the Suit being No.163 of 2004 filed by added respondent No.2 of Appeal No.17 of 1992 analogously giving chance to all the parties to amend their pleadings and to adduce evidence to prove their respective case. 

19. The stay order passed earlier by this Court hereby vacated. 

20. Let a copy of this judgment and order along with lower Courts record be sent to the concerned Court for information and necessary action.

End.

Mr. A.K.M. Shahidul Huq , j :- The impugned order No.19 dated 19.08.1997 of the learned Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia passed in Title Suit No.102 of 1990 has been called in question by invoking the revisional jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court on laying a petition under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure whereupon a Single Judge of this Hon'ble Division on perusal of the same was placed to issue a rule calling upon the opposite party Nos.1-4 to show cause as to why the impugned order of the learned Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia passed in Title Suit No.102 of 1990 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The short facts for disposal of the Rule are as follows:

On 25.09.1990 the present petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.102 of 1990 in the Assistant Judge Court, Kumarkhali for declaration of title and confirmation of possession against the predecessor-in-interest of the opposite party Nos.1-4, Kulsum Nessa.

3. The specific case of the plaintiff in short is that the suit land originally belonged to Kulsum Nessa. Plaintiff is the brother's son of Kulsum Nessa. Kulsum Nessa was issueless. Kulsum Nessa transferred 39 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff by way of registered gift deed dated 20.01.1973 and delivered possession. Defendant threatened to dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land through other person as a result the plaintiff filed the suit.

4. The summons was served upon the defendant but the defendant did not file any written statement as a result of which the learned Assistant Judge fixed the case on 10.07.1991 for exparte hearing. On that date  the defendant did neither appear nor take any step as a result of which the suit was decreed exparte on 10.07.1991.

5. After the death of Kulsum Nessa the present opposite party Nos.1-4 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.30 of 1994 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia against the present petitioner as defendant for setting aside the exparte decree dated 10.07.1991 passed in Title Suit No.102 of 1990.

6. The learned Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia was pleased to decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 26.02.1995 in Title Suit No.30 of 1994.

7. Against the judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali the present petitioner as appellant preferred Title Appeal No.43 of 1995 in the Court of District Judge, Kushtia, the same was heard by the learned subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Kushtia and was pleased to disallow the appeal by her judgment and decree dated 26.04.1997.

8. After disposal of appeal the plaintiff of Title Suit No.102 of 1990 filed an application on 04.08.1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali for starting the proceeding of Title Suit No.102 of 1990. But the learned Court did not pass any order on the application of the plaintiff dated 04.08.1997.

9. The plaintiff-petitioner filed another verified application dated 19.08.1997 for calling the records of Title Suit No.102 of 1990 and praying for hearing along with the earlier application dated 04.08.1997.

10. The learned Assistant Judge by his Order No.19 dated 19.08.1997 was pleased to order that - “ গত ০৪/০৮/১৯৯৭ ইং তারিখের দরখাস্ত শুনানীর জন্য লওয়া হইল। শুনিলাম। প্রার্থনা আইন সম্মত নহে। দরখাস্তটি নথিভূক্ত হউক।

11. Mr. Md. Saidul Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that once an application is filed by any party the Court must dispose of the same on merit. He further submits that there are 4 remedies against the exparte decree (1) A Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the original Suit. (2) An appeal to the higher Court under Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, (3) A review under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure and (4) a separate suit for setting aside the exparte decree. In that view of the matter the learned Assistant Judge committed a serious error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner further submits that the impugned order dated 19.08.1997 is a non speaking order and is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the impugned order is self contradictory the reason is that he himself stated that the application is unlawful but no explanation is given as to why it is unlawful while passing the impugned order he simply kept the application in the records of the suit. The learned Judge feel into gross error in not passing any order on the application and thus the impugned order suffers from serious miscarriage of justice resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the impugned order is a non speaking order. He also submits that the impugned order is not a proper order and thus deserves interference under the provision of law as contained in Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his contention he refers to the case of Jahura Bibi and others -Vs- Mvi. Habibur Rahman and other reported in 15 BLD (AD) 519 where their lordships held that ;

"In passing any judicial order the Court should assign reasons in its support. This is essential to enable the superior courts and the litigant public to see as to how a Sub-ordinate Court exercised its judicial mind in passing the order in question. The High Court Division is of the view that the learned Courts below shall not exercise their judicial discretion by mute or non-speaking orders in slipshod manners."

The learned Advocate for the petitioner in course of his submission also refers to the case of Anowar Hossain (Chunnu) and others Vs. Abdur Rashid Howlader and others reported in 15 BLD (HC) Page - 442 where his lordship held ;

"against and exparte decree 4 kinds of relief are available to the aggrieved party viz : (1) a miscellaneous case under order 9 rule-13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, (2) an appeal to the Higher Court, (3) a review under order 47 rule 1 of Code of Civil Procedure and (4) a separate suit for setting aside the exparte decree also placed the relevant provision of law as contained in Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the exparte decree. The provision is that "in any case in which a decree is passed exparte against a defendant, he may apply to the Court by which the decree was passed for an order to set it aside: and if he satisfies the Court that the summons was not duly served, or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing the Court shall make an order setting aside the decree as passed against him upon such terms as to cost, payment in to Court or otherwise as it thinks fit and shall appoint a day for proceeding with the suit".

12. On the other hand Mr. Muhammad Rezaul Kabir Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties on perusal of the impugned order frankly conceded to the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and he finds it difficult to support the impugned order.

13. Heard the learned Advocate perused the Revisional application filed under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure the impugned order considered submissions of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and also perused the citation as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner in course of his submission and consider the submission of the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties who in course of his submission frankly conceded to the submissions of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner.

<u>14. On consideration of the submission of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and on perusal of the citation as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner in support of his contention I find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. The impugned order passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge-in-charge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia dated 19.8.1997 in Title Suit No.102 of 1990 is absolutely a non speaking order and in my view it is no order in the eye of law and the same deserves interference under the Revisional jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Assistant Judge without disposing of the application on merit cannot keep the matter pending for an indefinite period by simply observing `শুনিলাম। প্রার্থনা আইন সম্মত নহে। দরখাস্তটি নথিভূক্ত হউক।' This sort of order is ex-facie illegal, misconceived order and also no order in the eye of law. The learned Assistant Judge in passing the impugned order committed  serious illegality and miscarriage of justice which deserves interference under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same is liable to be set aside. In that view of the matter the impugned order dated 19.8.1997 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge-in-charge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia in Title Suit No.102 of 1990 is hereby set aside.</u>

15. In the Result the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

16. The learned Assistant Judge, Kumarkahli, Kushtia is hereby directed to restore the Title Suit No.102 of 1990 to its original file and number after vacating the exparte order and proceed with the trial of Title Suit No.102 of 1990 in accordance with law.

17. Since it is a very old suit of 1990, the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia is hereby directed to dispose of the suit expeditiously preferably within 4 (four) months from the date of receipt of the lower Courts record.

18. Send down the L.C.R. along with a copy of this judgment to the concerned Court at once for information and necessary action.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule have been issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 05.07.2005 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 48 of 1994 reversing the judgment and order dated 13.07.1994 dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 79 of 1986 under Order IX rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte preliminary decree dated 25.11.1958 and final decree dated 30.12.1977 of Title Suit No. 214 of 1957 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge) 1st  Court, Barisal should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus that the defendant No.3 of Title Suit No. 214 of 1957 of the 1st Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Barisal filed a miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 17.12.1980 for setting aside the exparte preliminary decree dated 25.11.1958 which was made final on 30.12.1977 contending inter alia, that no summons of the above partition suit was served upon him and the plaintiffs to the suit in collusion with the process server of the court managed to obtain a false service return and after fraudulent service of summons practicing fraud upon the court the plaintiffs obtained the preliminary decree behind the back of the defendant No.3 to the original suit. The defendant No.3 who is the petitioner of the miscellaneous case was in the dark about the existence of the suit which was filed against him and others. For the first time on 02.12.1986 the defendant-petitioner came to know about the decree from one Sirajul Hoque Sharif. Thereafter, the defendant no.3 being petitioner preferred the miscellaneous case for setting aside the exparte decree obtained against him fraudulently. 

3. The contrary case of the plaintiff-opposite party No.I 9 of the case in brief is such that the summons was duly served upon the petitioner, who was the defendant no.3 to the original partition suit and the petitioner is in no way prejudiced by the impugned judgment and decree but only to harass the plaintiff he filed the miscellaneous case on false allegation. 

4. The learned trial court i.e. the 1st court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal by his judgment and order dated 13.07.1994 dismissed the miscellaneous case and being aggrieved the defendant-petitioner preferred a miscellaneous appeal in the court of learned District Judge, Barisal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 48 of 1994 which was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal and the learned appellate court below by the impugned judgment and order dated 05.07.2005 allowed the miscellaneous appeal reversing the judgment and order passed by the learned trial court and set aside the exparte preliminary decree dated 25.11.1958. 

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order the heir of the plaintiff-opposite party- respondent has preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay. 
6. Mr. Swapan Kumar Dutta, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioner while Mr. Md. Enamul Hoque the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties. 

7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the appellate court below during disposal of the miscellaneous appeal committed illegality and irregularity in holding that the summons of the original suit was suppressed upon the defendant-petitioner and the defendant-petitioner was in the dark about the existence of the partition suit filed against him and others. The learned Advocate further submits that under the provisions of section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, 1872 it has got a presumptive value that the process server of the court duly served the summons notice upon the defendant-petitioner and nothing has been suppressed. In allowing the appeal the learned lawyer appellate court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was hopelessly time barred and the petitioner to the case was not in a position to prove his date of knowledge as alleged in the contents of the application. The only witness of the petitioner not corroborated the petitioner during his deposition before the trial court and the learned lower appellate court misconstrued the decision reported in 35 DLR(AD)162. 

8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the grounds mentioned by the learned counsel for the petitioner and submits that in the original partition suit the petitioner of the miscellaneous case was the defendant no.3 and he was quite in the dark about the existence of the suit which was filed against him. The service of summons is collusive, fraudulent and it was suppressed by the concerned process-server of the court in collusion with the plaintiff to the suit and practicing fraud upon the court the plaintiff-opposite party obtained the preliminary decree which was exparte against the defendant-petitioner. The learned Advocate further submits that because of the suppression of summons the date of knowledge of the defendant-petitioner is immaterial and the learned lower appellate court was quite justified in relying upon the decision of our Apex Court reported in 35 DLR(AD)162. The learned Advocate further submits that the allegation which was set-forth by the defendant-petitioner in his miscellaneous case was not challenged by the plaintiff-opposite party during hearing of the miscellaneous case. The defendant-petitioner was not even cross-examined from the side of the plaintiff to controvert or falsify the specific assertion of the defendant no.3 of the original suit. As such the testimony of the defendant-petitioner remained unchallenged, which amounts to admission from the side of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the appellate court below after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law rightly decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the defendant-appellant and there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Barisal. 

9. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the impugned judgment and order along with the judgment and order passed by the trial court in Miscellaneous Case being No. 79 of 1986 under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the judgment and decree passed on 15.11.1958, which was finally disposed of in the form of final decree on 30.12.1977. 

10. On perusal of the connected papers, it transpires that the petitioner to the miscellaneous case was the defendant no.3 to the original' suit which was disposed of against him exparte. It is the clear contention of the defendant-petitioner that he was not in the know about the existence of the suit filed against him and the summons notice was suppressed fraudulently by the process-server of the court in collusion with the plaintiff to the suit. By practicing fraud upon the court the decree was obtained exparte against the defendant-petitioner and the defendant-petitioner knowing about the decree passed against him for the first time on 02.12.1986 preferred the miscellaneous case for setting aside the judgment and decree passed against him. 

11. On careful scrutiny over the papers it is apparent that the learned trial court during disposal of the miscellaneous case examined two witnesses from the side of the defendant-petitioner therein and no witness was produced from the side of the plaintiff-opposite parties. It appears from the records that the defendant-petitioner, who was examined as witness No.1 was not cross-examined from the side of the plaintiff-opposite party. It was asserted by the defendant-petitioner in his deposition that he was not in the know about the suit filed against him and he did not receive any summons of the Court. The process-server of the court did not serve any summons notice upon him as alleged and the service return as it appears is collusive and fraudulent. The learned trial court at the time of disposal of the miscellaneous case is misconceived in holding the basic criterion of the case under order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The pertinent question is as to whether the service of summons was properly done or not. Apparently; the trial court without going into the merit of the service return banked upon the deposition of the witness No.2 for the petitioner from whom the petitioner for the first time allegedly came to know about the exparte decree. 

12. We have come across from the connected documents that the contention of the petitioner as stated by him in his examination-in-chief was not contradicted or challenged from the side of the plaintiff-opposite party. The plaintiff-opposite party remained silent despite he filed the written objection initially against the pleading of the defendant-petitioner. In this context this Bench decided in a case law reported in 18 BLC 386 in the case of Shamir Chandra Sawjal and others —vs.- Government of Bangladesh that the failure of cross-examine the plaintiff's witness to falsify the case of the plaintiff or controvert the positive assertion of the witness as appears from his examination-in-chief tantamounts to admission from the side of the defendant. In giving the aforesaid decision this Bench relied upon the decision of our Apex Court in the case of Abdur Rashid —vs.- Alz.al Kazi reported in 16 MLR(AD)4. 

13. Furthermore, once when the defendant denies the service of summons upon him; the whole onus shifts to the plaintiff to prove that in-fact summons was duly served and that is the decision of our Appellate Division in several case laws reported in 16 BLD(AD)4, 1 BLC(AD)179 and when the Court is satisfied that there was no due service of summons, it is bound to set aside the ex-perte decree and in that case knowledge is immaterial (Ref. 35 DLR (AD)162; 4 BLD (AD) 83; 1983 BCR (AD) 207 and 12 BLC (AD) 75). 

14. Besides this; it is the established principle of civil law that the knowledge about institution of the suit does not dispense with the requirement of service of summons. If summons is not served on the defendant the decree is liable to be set aside, even if the defendants knew about the institution of the suit. 
15. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions made above, I am constrained to hold such a view that the learned lower appellate court was quite justified in allowing the miscellaneous appeal and rightly reversed the judgment and order passed by the trial court. 

16. In the result, the Rule having no merit is discharged without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order dated 05.07.2005 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 48 of 1994 reversing the judgment and order dated 13:07.1994 dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 79 of 1986 under Order IX rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte preliminary decree dated 25.11.1958 and final decree dated 30.12.1977 of Title Suit No. 214 of 1957 is hereby affirmed. 

17. The order of stay granted earlier at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated. 

18. Communicate the judgment and order at once. 
End.
