full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule have been issued calling upon the Principle-Opposite Party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 12.09.1992 and 19.09.1992 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st  Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 115 of 1987 affirming the judgment and decree dated 26.02.1987 and 05.03.1987 respectively passed by the learned Munsif, Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 73 of 1986 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell, can be stated thus, the plaintiff-opposite party filed the original suit being title suit no. 368 of 1984 in the 1st Court of the then Munsif, Dhaka which was transferred to the Additional Court of Munsif and renumbered as Title Suit No. 73 of 1986 for declaration and permanent injunction contending inter alia that the plaintiff is a bonafide business man who purchased the possession of the suit shop from one Md. Selim at a consideration of Tk. 30,000/- (thirty thousand) on 19.12.1979 and since then he is running his business as a shop of cycle and cycle parts. The plaintiff is a member of Mohammadpur Bazar Committee under Dhaka Metropolitan Area and during the continuance of plaintiff's possession a litigation was cropped up between the market committee and the shop-keepers regarding the recognition of the possessors in the shops. Several meetings were held between the market committee and the representative of the shop-keepers in presence of concerned minister in charge and it was decided that a survey team after physical survey would prepare a list of businessman who are found in occupation of the shops. Accordingly, a survey team was constituted and after survey they .submitted a report to the concern ministry of the Government on 16.03.1981 and the plaintiff's name was listed in serial no. 19. Before final publication of the said list a subsequent survey was held on a dispute by a legally constituted survey team and in the said survey report which was published finally in the year 1984 the name of the plaintiff has been enlisted in serial no. 24. On the basis of that final list the defendant no. 1 who is the Administrative officer, Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Mohammadpur, Dhaka issued an offer letter in favour of the plaintiff on 07.06.1984 asking the plaintiff to deposit Tk. 30,000/-(thirty thousand) as compensation and arrear rent of the suit shop in 3(three) instalments in order to get allotment of the shop. Accordingly the plaintiff paid Tk. 15,000/-(fifteen thousand) of first installment within the prescribed time on 10.06.1984. But on the same date the plaintiff received a letter showing that his allotment offer was issued on mistake and therefore it was cancelled. Being aggrieved by that letter the plaintiff filed the original suit. 

3. The contrary case of the contesting defendant is such that the suit-shop is a Government shop at Mohammadpur area which is controlled and managed by the defendants. The defendant no.1 out of mistake issued an offer letter under memo no. 291/A.O. dated 07.06.1984 and after investigation it was found that the letter was issued out of mistake which was cancelled accordingly. The plaintiff was merely asked to deposit Tk. 30,000/- (thirty thousand) as compensation money and the issuance of offer letter does not confer any right, title and interest of the suit-shop in favour of the plaintiff. The Government considering the actual facts issued offer letter to one Mrs. Aftab Uddin Ahmed who is the defendant-respondent-petitioner of this revisional application vide memo no. 316/A.O. dated 10.06.1984. The further case of the contesting defendant is such that the plaintiff is a trespasser in the suit-shop and he has no legal right for getting the allotment letter of the suit shop and the letter of cancellation of the offer of allotment is quite lawful and the plaintiff is not entitled to get relief as prayed for. The learned the then Munsif, Additional Court, Dhaka vide his judgment and decree dated 26.02.1987 decreed the suit in part and declared the letter of cancellation dated 10.06.1984 illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. Being aggrieved the defendant preferred a Title Appeal in the court of learned District Judge, Dhaka being Title Appeal No. 115 of 1987 which was heard and disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge, Is' Court, Dhaka. The learned appellate court after hearing the appeal disallowed the same affirming the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 05.03.1987. 

4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree of the learned Appellate Court the Defendant-appellant-petitioner has preferred this revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule. 

5. Mr. Md. A.K. Shamsuddin, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioner while Mr. Md. Shahidul Islam, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite party. 

6. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and subsequent appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity in deciding the fate of the suit and appeal respectively in favour of the plaintiff. The learned advocate further submits that the part decree of the trial court and the judgment of affirmation by the appellate court below are illegal, invalid and ultravires. The learned court below failed to determine that the plaintiff have got no prima-facie case and right, title, interest in the suit-shop and the issuance of allotment offer by the authority in favour of the plaintiff was a mistake and as soon as the matter was brought into the notice of the concerned authority they cancelled the offer letter which was earlier inadvertently issued in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party. The learned advocate further submits that no title and interest was 'conferred in favour of the plaintiff by issuance of the allotment offer letter and accordingly no contract was effected between the parties. The learned appellate court below misinterpreted the law and failed to assess the evidence on record properly and accordingly committed an error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned advocate for the petitioner lastly submits that the witness no. 1 for the plaintiff Md. Monjur Alam was not legally empowered to depose in favour of the plaintiffs case and his deposition bears no value in the eye of law which is barred under Order III Rule 1 and 2 of the, Code of Civil Procedure. The learned lower appellate court as well as the trial court without considering the very aspect committed illegality and as such the impugned judgment and decree deserve interference of this court. 

7. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and it's subsequent appeal committed no illegality or irregularity and there is no non-consideration of the material facts and non-reading or misreading of evidence resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned advocate also submits that the defendant in support of his respective case has totally failed to produce any scrap of authentic paper to substantiate his claim in the Suit-shop. The learned advocate further submits that the plaintiff is a bonafide purchaser of possession of suit-shop and in the year 1979 A.D. the plaintiff purchased the possession of the shop from the original owner Mohammad Salim and he is continuing his business therein as a shop of cycle and cycle parts since then. In the year 1981 and 1984 there were two field survey physically by a legally constituted survey team and in both the two survey it was found that the plaintiff do possess the suit-shop and use to run his business therein. The survey teams rightly submitted their report and in first Report in serial no. 19 and in the subsequent Report in serial no. 24 the name of the plaintiff has been enlisted. The Government finding the legal aspect and physical possession of the suit-shop issue an offer of allotment letter and asked the plaintiff to deposit the consideration money. Accordingly., the, plaintiff deposited his first installment within time but subsequently in an arbitrarily and malafide way the defendant no. 1 being influenced by third party issued a cancellation letter stating 'mistake' without any specification and the plaintiff thereafter to redress his grievances filed the original suit which is thoroughly considered by both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and appeal. The learned advocate lastly submits that the appellate court being the final court of fact committed no wrong and rightly assessed the evidence on record properly. The witness no. 1 for the plaintiff Md. Monjur Alam being the father of the plaintiff was quite competent and legally empowered to depose on behalf of his son and under the purview of Order III Rule 2(b) this witness legally deposed in support of the respective case of the plaintiff and hence; there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court. 

8. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, perused the case record, exhibited documents, findings and discussions of the learned courts below, deposition of the witnesses and all other connected papers. 

9. On perusal of the case record it transpires that the suit-shop is situated within Mohammadpur area and admittedly the plaintiff-opposite party possess the suit-shop since 1979. It is the case of the defendant that the possession of the plaintiff is unauthorized and he is a trespasser in the suit-shop. I have come across from the evidence on records that the plaintiff Mahmud Alam alias Mahmudul Alam purchased the possession of the suit-shop from one Mohammad Selim in the year 1979. The documentary evidence dated 19.12.1979 has been marked as 'exhibit-1'. The survey report of Mohammadpur Government market and list of market committee which has been marked as 'exhibit-2' supported the case of the plaintiff as to the enlistment of his name as possessor of the suit-shop. Both the courts below in their findings and decisions opined that the possession of the plaintiff in the suit-shop has been reflected by the documents produced and from two legally empowered survey committees for twice the contention of the plaintiff established. Accordingly, the Administrative officer of Mohammadpur Housing Estate issued an offer letter of allotment of the suit-shop in favour of the plaintiff vide memo no. 291/A.O. dated 07.06.1984. Pursuant to the said letter the plaintiff deposited his first installment of Tk. 15,000/- (fifteen thousand) on 10.06.1984 in favour of Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka. On the same date i.e. on 10.06.1984 the disputed cancellation letter was issued by the said authority stating that out of mistake the earlier offer letter of allotment was issued in respect of the suit-shop which was signed by the officer concerned on 07.06.1984 but curiously the memo was issued on 10.06.1984. 1 have come across from the documentary evidence which has been marked as 'exhibit-6' that a title suit being no. 532 of 1974 in which the order of statusquo was passed was dismissed on 01.01.1976. Subsequent to that a miscellaneous case being no. 129 of 1975 was filed for restoration of the suit which was also dismissed for default on 30.04.1984. 

10. Never the less; a separate miscellaneous case being no. 83 of 1984 was instituted 
under Order IX Rule 9 of the Code of Civil .Procedure on 10.05.1984 but there is nothing to show that the case was allowed or the original suit was restored to it's file and number. Therefore, it is evident to note that the order of status quo was no more in existence while the offer letter was issued in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party. On careful scrutiny over the evidence on record it further appears that the witness no. I for the plaintiff corroborated the plaint case and it has come to the notice of the court that at the relevant time the son of this witness the plaintiff was residing at Chittagong and the witness no. 1 Monjur Alam looked after the suit shop and used to run the business therein. He is well acquainted with the suit-shop from the very beginning. The witness no. 2 for the plaintiff is Mirza Mahmud Hasan who is the president of the market committee and in the year 1975 A.D. executive member of the said market committee states at a stage that one Aftab Uddin possessed the suit shop from 1973 to 1975 and thereafter leaving the suit-shop he left the place. This witness also states that the market committee and housing settlement concern to ascertain and recognize the genuine business man who possess the shops surveyed the shops of the market after forming a survey committee and during both the two survey period it was found that the plaintiff is in possession in the suit-shop. This witness also states in his deposition that the plaintiff 'deposited the amount first. The only witness for the defendants is the witness no. 1 Md. Nur Jamal who is an upper division Assistant of housing settlement under Ministry of Housing and Settlement. This witness states specifically at a stage of his testimony that they issued the offer letter in favour of the plaintiff on 07.06.1984 and that letter was cancelled on 10.07.1984. This witness admits that vide exhibit- B and B/1 the plaintiff deposited Tk. 15,000/- (fifteen thousand) as compensation in compliance of their offer letter for allotment. In the cross-examination the sole witness of the defendants in the very beginning states in the following way: একজিবিট-২ এবং ২(এ) সার্ভে রিপোর্ট আমাদের ডিপার্টমেন্ট কর্তৃক করা হয়েছে এবং সার্ভে রিপোর্ট অনুযায়ী অফার লেটার দেই। উক্ত সার্ভে রিপোর্ট এ যারা দখলে আছে তাদের নাম এবং তারা কবে থেকে দখলে আছে তা উল্লেখ আছে।" In another stage of his deposition this witness states, ‘‘দুটি সার্ভে রিপোর্ট এ বাদী দখলে আছে বিধায় অফার লেটার দিয়েছিলাম। সার্ভে রিপোর্ট অনুযায়ী দখলকারীদেরকে অফার লেটার দেয়া হয়েছি। বে-দখলকারীদের অফার লেটার দেয়া হয় নাই।" 
11. From the aforesaid admission of the sole witness for the defendants apparently it can be said that the witness concern falsified the defendant's case itself and it is not the case of the Government i.e. the appropriate authority that the plaintiff is a trespasser and he has got unauthorized possession in the suit-shop. The learned courts below during disposal of the suit as well as appeal rightly assessed the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties in its true perspective. Furthermore; it is noticed that the evidence were evaluated properly to address the actual matter in dispute. No such misreading and non-reading of 'evidence is noticed by which it can be held that the impugned judgment and decree suffers from any sort of illegality. 

12. The learned counsel on behalf of the petitioner in support of the defendant's pleadings referred a decision of this court reported in 4 BLC 197. Going through the said case law including the facts of the case along with the instant case I may not be out of place to advert that the said decision is not identical in our case. The connected provisions of law as contemplated in the instant nature of suit is guided by Order III Rule 2(b) of the Code of Civil Procedure; 

The principle of law is such that the Person carrying on trade or business for and in the name of a party who is not resident within the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court within which limits the appearance, application or act is made or done, in matters connected with such trade or business only, where no other agent is expressly authorized to make and do such appearances, applications and acts is legally empowered to depose; as the instant case be. 

13. During argument the learned advocate on behalf of the opposite party referred a decision. I have gone through the respective decision of our Court reported in 22 DLR 242. In the case of Hazi Sharafatullah vs. Deputy Commissioner, Dinajpur and others. Relying upon several decisions of our Apex Court this court opined that a show cause I notice is very much necessary for the principle of natural justice once his licence is granted and subsequently cancelled. I think; the said decision is very much applicable in the instant case. Be that as it. may; in this case the concerned authority as I have come across without giving any show cause notice or opportunity of being heard most arbitrarily issued the subsequent cancellation letter which is the high handedness of the department concerned and not at-all desirable. It is a fact that the contract between the parties has already been fulfilled after payment of part consideration as first installment by a `Chalan' in favour of Housing Society by the plaintiff-opposite party. The learned courts below committed no illegality in holding that under the purview of Contract Act the contract between the parties have already been held and the act done by the plaintiff was in accordance with law. Section 2(a) of the Contracts Act is very much clear in this context which was rightly considered by both the courts below. 

14. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and evidence referred to above I have every reason to incline such a view that the Rule have got no substance to succeed. 

15. In the result; the Rule is discharged. 

16. The impugned judgment and decree dated 12.09.1992 and 19.09.1992 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 115 of 1987 affirming those of dated 26.02.1987 and 05.03.1987 respectively passed by the learned Munsif, Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 73 of 1986 is hereby affirmed. 

17. However, there will be no order as to costs.

lawyer:
Mr. Md. Harunur Rashid, Advocate ------ For the Petitioner
Mr. Joynul Abedin With Mr. Md. Sagir Hossein. Advocates ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Md. Nasurullah alias Nasu ------ Petitioner
Versus
Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Quddus, J.:- This Rule, at the instance of a legal heir of a judgment debtor in a mortgage decree, was issued calling in question the proceeding in Execution Case No. 727 of 2005 of Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka and the legality of order dated 7.8.2007 passed therein rejecting an application for release of the auctioned property on paument of the decretal money.

2. Facts leading to this writ petition, in short, are that the Islami Bank Ltd, Mirpur, Branch, Dhaka as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No.777 of 2004 in. Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka for recovery of loan amounting, to Taka 6, 69,706/= (six lac sixty-nine thousand seven hundred six) only against the petitioner's parents Tannur Ali and Nasira Bibi. The suit was ultimately decreed ex-parte on 22.3.2005 (decree signed on 29 3.2005) giving 60 (sixty) days-time to the judgment debtors to pay the decretal amount in favour of the decree holder-bank. As the judgment debtors failed to pay the decretal amount, the bank put the decree in execution by filing Artha Jail Case No.727 of 2005 on 27.10.2005. In course of proceedings in the said execution case, the mortgaged property was put in auction on 31.7.2006 and the highest bid of Taka 7,70,000/= (seven lac seventy thousand) only was accepted 

3. The petitioner's father being a judgment debtor came to learn about the auction sale and filed Miscellaneous Case No 29 of 2007 for setting aside the ex-parte decree depositing 10% of the decretal amount, but it was dismissed. Being aggrieved by the said order of dismissal, he preferred Artha Rin Appeal No.4 of 2007 depositing 40% of the decretal amount. The learned Judge of the appellate Court heard the appeal and dismissed the same by his judgment and order dated 23.5.2007. Thereafter the judgment debtor (petitioner's father) filed an application on 9.7.2007 before the executing Court for depositing the remaining decreta amount and release the property.. The executing Court, upon the said application, directed him to deposit Taka 2;00,000/. (Taka two lac) only and deferred hearing of the application on 13.7.2007. On the next date (15.7.2007) the judgment debtor filed another application for depositing remaining portion of the decretal amount, which the executing Court allowed and fixed 7.8.2007 for hearing of the application. In pursuance of the said order dated 15.7.2007, the judgment debtor deposited Taka 1,35,000/= (one lac thirty-five thousand) only as the remaining portion of the decretal amount, and that he deposited the entire decretal amount. The learned Judge of the executing Court ultimately heard the application and rejected it by order dated 7.8.2007. 

4. Being aggrieved by the said execution proceeding and order dated 7.8.2007 passed therein, the petitioner has moved this Court and obtained the Rule on 7.2.2010. During pendency of the Rule, the petitioner filed three applications: one for addition of the auction purchaser as respondent No.4, another for issuance of the Rule against him and the last one for injunction, which the Court allowed by order dated 19.8.2010 and added the auction purchaser as respondent No.4 issuing a Rule upon him, and also directed the parties to maintain statuesque in respect of possession and position of the property in question. Thereafter respondent Nos.5-7 filed another application for addition of party claiming themselves as subsequent purchasers from the auction purchaser, which was also allowed by order dated 9.12.2010. 

5. The added respondent Nos.5-7 have appeared and contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia, that the execution case was filed well within time; that the auction was held on 31.7.2006 i.e long before passing of the impugned order on 7.8.2007; that the auction purchaser had taken possession over the auctioned property and the execution case was disposed of on 18.2.2009; that subsequently the auction purchaser transferred the same to these respondents on 14.10.2009; that the petitioner obtained the instant Rule and order of statuesque suppressing the material facts. 

6. Mr. Md. Hamm- Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has supported the Rule and submitted that section 28 (1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 provides special limitation of 180 days for filing an execution case, from the date of passing the executable decree. In the present case decree, was passed on 22.3,2005 and execution case was filed on 27.10.2005 i.e after expiry of 180 days and as such it is hopelessly bared by limitation. The auction held in an illegal execution proceeding is also illegal and it did not create any right and title over the mortgaged property in favour of the auction purchaser. Since the mortgaged property is the only homestead of the judgment debtor, the executing Court ought to have accepted his application and released the property. Moreover the executing Court allowed the judgment debtor to- deposit the entire decretal amount, but ultimately rejected his application for release of the mortgaged property by the impugned order and thereby sat over its own judgment, which it cannot do. In support, the learned Advocate cited the case of Khorihed Alam —Vs- Sub Ordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat  No. 1 and others, reported in 54 DLR, 239. 

7. On the other hand, Mr. Joynul Abedin, the learned Advocate appearing for added respondent Nos.5-7, submits that the execution case in question is well within time in view of section 29 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, which provides that the  limitation for filing an execution case would  not run during the time given in a decree. In  present case the decree was passed with  a direction upon the judgment debtors to pay  the decretal amount in favour of the decree holder-bank within 60 (sixty) days and therefore the limitation would run after expiry of 60 (sixty) days from signing the decree on 29.3.2005. 
8. The learned Advocate further submits that meanwhile the auction sale had been confirmed and the sale certificate was also registered. Subsequently the auction purchaser sold the property to these respondents, who went into possession over the auctioned property, got the record mutated in their names and paid rem and development taxes to the respective land office. The petitioner has obtained the Rule on 7.2.2010 after long laps of two and half years from passing the impugned order on 7.8.2007 and suppressed the materials facts and as such the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

9. We have perused the writ petition, application for injunction, affidavit—in-opposition and documents submitted therewith, and also have gone through the decision cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. 

10. In 54 DLR, 239 an executing Court had accepted negotiated auction price on an application filed by the decree holder-bank in an execution case under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. Subsequently the executing Court set aside its previous order of acceptance of the negotiated price, challenging which the auction purchaser obtained Rule in a writ petition. After hearing of the Rule, the High Court Division made it absolute in part on the ground among others that "the some Court cannot sit over its own judgment in the facts of the present case." The facts and circumstances in the present case are quite different, and there is no such order by which the executing Court has set aside any of its previous orders passed in the present execution case. Therefore the case cited by the learned Advocate is distinguishable. 

11. It appears from the decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No.777 of 2004 that it was signed on 29.3.2005 giving 60 (sixty) days-time to the judgment debtors to pay off the decretal amount in favour of the decree holder-bank (vide annexe: A-2 to the writ petition). In view of section 29 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, limitation of filing the application for execution of the decree in the present case, would run after expiry of 60 (sixty) days from 29.3.2005. Admittedly the present execution case was filed on 27.10.2005 and on calculation of limitation it appears to have been filed within 180 days after expiry of 60 (sixty) days from passing the decree. Therefore we do not find any substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner on limitation.

12. It further appears from the order sheet of the execution case in question (vide annexes: H and I to the application for injunction) that after observance of all necessary legal formalities the auction was held on 31.7.2006 and the highest bid of Tulsa 7, 70,000/= quoted by respondent No.4 was accepted; respondent No.4 paid the full consideration to the executing Court on 9.8.2006; the sale was confirmed on 3.9.2006, sale certificate (boinama) was issued on 27.11.2006 and it was registered on 30.11.2006; after long laps of time, the judgment debtor (petitioner's father) filed an unusual application on 9.7.2007 for release of the auctioned property on payment of the remaining decretal amount; the learned Judge of the executing Court* though allowed him to deposit the remaining decretal amount, but ultimately rejected his application by the impugned order dated 7.82007 on the ground that there is no scope in law to redeem the property at this stage (vide annexe-G to the writ petition). 

13. It also appears from the said order sheet that the writ of possession was returned to the executing Court on 9.9.2007. As the decree was fully satisfied with delivery of possession,. the decree holder-bank or the auction purchaser did not take any interest to pursue the execution case, as a result it was rejected for default on 18.2.2009. Thereafter the judgment debtor filed another similar application on 25.2.2008, which was also rejected by order dated 18.3,2009. Meanwhile the auction purchaser sold the property in question to added respondents No.5-7 on 14.10.2009, who mutated the record in their names and paid rent to the land office (vide annexes:3 and 3-I to the affidavit-in-opposition). As the present writ petitioner has stepped into the shoe of his father, there is no scope for him to take the plea that he was not aware of the subsequent development of the execution proceedings. Moreover the facts subsequent to order dated 7.8.2007 have been suppressed in the writ petition. In the instant Rule the proceedings of an execution case has been challenged, which is already disposed of. The judgment debtor did not file any Civil Revision under section 42 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain challenging the judgment and order dated 23.5.2007 passed in Artha Rin Appeal No.4 of 2007. During enforcement of the said judgment and order there is no scope in law to establish the fact that he had no knowledge of the Artha Rin Suit. 

14. In view of the above, we do not find any substance in the Rule. Accordingly the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to costs. The order of statuesque passed on 19.8.2010 by this Court is hereby vacated. The executing Court is directed to return the money as deposited by the judgment debtor in accordance with law. 

15. Before parting with the case we put it on records that the learned Judge of the executing Court allowed the judgment debtor to deposit the decretal amount beyond the scope of law and created a false hope in his mind that he may get back his property. Such an illegal order of the executing Court would not create any right for redemption of the mortgaged property in favour of the judgment debtor. This is a well settled principle of law that after confirmation of sale of any mortgaged property in due process of law, the mortgagor loses his all rights and interest over the property. 

16. Let a copy of the judgment be communicated to the concerned executing Court for future guidance as well.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Borhanuddin, J.:- This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party no. 1 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 22.02.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge 1st Court, Habigonj, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 49 of 2005 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 14.08.2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Habigonj, in Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 2002, should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule, in short, are that opposite party no.1 herein as plaintiff instituted Title Suit no. 5 of 1994 for partition and khas possession of suit land claiming that she purchased the suit schedule land from defendant no.1. Suit was decreed in preliminary form which was also upheld by this Division. This petitioner, defendant no.2 of the Title Suit, filed an application for pre-emption under Section 4 of the Partition Act. contending inter alia that defendant no.9 of the suit is his aunt and he purchased share of his aunt and got delivery of possession; opposite party decree holder is an stranger in the suit land; this petitioner has been living with his family on 1/2 sataks of the suit land by erecting houses therein; suit land is an ejmali homestead and as such the petitioner being co-sharer filed instant miscellaneous case to purchase portion of ejmali property transferred to the plaintiff-opposite party no.1.

3. Opposite party no. 1 contested the case by filing written objection contending inter alia that defendant no. 12 of the Suit to serve his own purpose filed instant miscellaneous case through the petitioner; One decimal land from Suit schedule Plot transferred to the opposite party no. 12 vide kabala dated 27.07.1993 and oil the same date this petitioner along with his mother and sister i.e. opposite party nos. 3, 4 and 7 sold 41 decimals of land to the opposite party nos. 10 and 11 which was admitted by the petitioner in his written statement filed in Title Suit no. 5 of 1994; Contention of the petitioner that no land has been transferred from suit plot no.8088 is not true and as such the petitioner is not entitled to get pre-emption under Section 4 of the partition act. The petitioner filed instant miscellaneous case only to deprive the opposite party-decree holder from enjoying fruit of the decree obtained in Title Suit no.5 of 1994.

4. After hearing the parties, learned Senior Assistant Judge, Hobigonj has been pleased 6o reject the case on contest against opposite party no. 1 and ex-parte against the rest vide judgment and order dated 14.08.2005 holding that the suit land is not ejmali property inasmuch as PW.1 in his cross examination admitted that some portion of the suit land has already been transferred to the opposite party nos. 10 and 11 and he himself sold homestead and pond from suit plot no.8088 to the opposite party no.12.

5. Being aggrieved, the petitioner as appellant preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.49 of 2005 in the court of learned District Judge, Hobiganj, which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Hobiganj, who after hearing the parties has been pleased to dismiss the appeal by his judgment and order dated 22.02.2011.

6. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order, the petitioners, legal heirs of the deceased petitioner, preferred  this revisional application under Section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present rule and an order of status-quo.

7. Mr. Md. Zakir Hossain, learned advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that both the courts below committed an error of law in holding that the miscellaneous case under section 4 of the Partition Act., is not maintainable as the property not belongs to joint family without considering the legal aspect that the original suit has been filed for partition of ejmali property which is admittedly not partitioned by metes and bounds amongst the co-sharers. He also submits that both the courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the judgment and order without considering that the suit schedule homestead is ejmali property and the petitioners are co-sharers by purchase as well as by inheritance.

8. On the other hand, Mr. M. Mahbub Ali with Mr. M. A Mortuja, learned advocates appearing for the opposite party no.1 submits that the miscellaneous case is not maintainable inasmuch as the petitioner contested Title Suit No.5 of 1994 as defendant no.2 and the suit was decreed in preliminary form on 07.06.1998 which also upheld by this Division and ultimately final decree passed on 23.05.2012 since no one filed written objection. He also submits that instant miscellaneous case under Section 4 of the partition Act. is a device to deprive the opposite party-decree holder from enjoying fruit of the decree. He next submits that it is apparent from the judgment of the courts below that the petitioner himself admitted in cross examination as PW. 1 that a portion of the suit land has already been transferred to the opposite party nos. 10 and 11 and he himself sold homestead and pond from Suit Plot no.8088 to the opposite party

no.12, as such courts below rightly arrived at a concurrent finding that the suit schedule homestead not belongs to joint family.

9. Heard the learned advocate for the parties. Perused the application and judgment and order passed by the courts below.

10. Admittedly, this petitioner contested the suit as defendant no.2 in Title Suit No.5 of 1994 preferred by the opposite party no. I as plaintiff seeking partition and khas possession in the suit land. Said suit decreed in preliminary form on 07.06.1998 in favour of the opposite party no. 1 and the decree was upheld by this Division. Ultimately, said preliminary decree was ended up in the form of final decree.

<u>11. From the judgment and order passed by the courts below, it reveals that the petitioner in his cross examination as PW. 1 admitted that a portion of land from the suit schedule has already been transferred to the opposite party nos. 10 and 11 and he himself sold homestead and pond from Suit Plot no. 8088 to the defendant no. 12 of Title Suit No.5 of 1994. Both the courts below on assessing the evidence on record arrived at a concurrent finding that homestead of suit schedule is not ejmali property since a portion of the suit land has already been transferred to another stranger and the petitioner himself said homestead and pond from the Suit Plot to one Abdul Ahad which also corroborated by PW.2 Safar Ali who deposed that Abdul Ahad is living in the homestead of the suit schedule, these finding of facts by the courts below cannot be revised under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.</u>

12. Section 4 of the Partition Act provides that a member of an undivided family being

a share holder undertake to buy the share of transferee can file application under this Section on the following conditions:

"(I) the dwelling house belongs to an undivided family.

(II) a portion/share of that dwelling house has been transferred to a stranger i.e. not a member of the undivided family.

(III) transferee sues, partition.

"It is apparent that some portion of the homestead and land of suit schedule has already been transferred to the opposite party nos. 10 and 11 and the petitioner himself sold homestead and pond from Suit Plot no.8088 to the defendant no.12 of the Suit which is admitted by the petitioner in his cross examination as PW.1 and confirmed by the PW.2 in his deposition, as such I am of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled to get any relief under Section 4 of the Partition Act.

13. In such view of the matter, I do not find any merit in the Rule.

14. Accordingly, the Rule is discharged. Judgment and order dated 22.02.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge Court, Hobigonj, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 49 of 2005 dismissing the appeal, is maintained.

15. The order of status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the Rule and extended from time to time is hereby vacated.

16. Send a copy of this judgment to the court concern at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Nuruzzaman, J.:- The instant Rule was issued calling upon the judgment-debtor opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned Order dated 18.02.2010 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Money Execution Case No. 01 of 2009 rejecting decree-holder's application under Order XXI, rule 54(1) read with Section 46 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for attachment of the judgment debtor's property and for issuance of precepts to this effect, shall not be set aside.

2. The material facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, as has been stated in the revisional application, in short, are that the decree-holder-petitioner entered into 2 separate contracts dated 16.11.2000 and 14.02.2001 with the judgment-debtor-opposite party. In those contracts the parties incorporated the Rules of Arbitration as per bye-laws and rules of the Liverpool Cotton Association, agreeing to settle of their disputes arising out of the contracts through arbitration. Accordingly the disputes arose between the parties in respect of contracts and then it was referred to the Liverpool Cotton Association for Arbitration. The Arbitral Tribunal after hearing of the parties passed the award on 25.9.2002 in favour of the decree-holder. In pursuance of the award dated 25.9.2002 the Awardee on 30-8-2005 obtained an order from the Royal Courts of Justice, Admiralty and Commercial Registry, England to make the award Rule of the Court. Thereafter Awardee served a notice on 20.2.2006 through its local Counsel upon the judgment-debtor to comply and satisfy the aforesaid award. However, the judgment-debtor neither took any steps to set aside the award nor settled and satisfied with the said award. In the prevailing facts and circumstances the Awardee decree-holder for realisation of Award money filed Money Execution Case No.1 of 2009 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka, Bangladesh for execution of the award dated 25.9.2002. The learned District Judge registered the application as Money Execution Case No.1 of 2009 and started the execution proceeding by issuing summons upon the judgment-debtor.

3. While the said execution case was so pending, the Awardee decree-holder on 17.9.2009 by filing an application under Order 21, rule 54(1) read with Sections 46 and 151 of the Code Civil Procedure sought for attachment of the judgment-debtor's property located in the District Chuadanga and further prayed for an order for issuing precepts and send to the learned District Judge, Chuadanga for execution of the precept. The judgment-debtor appeared in the Money Execution Case and contested against the application for attachment and issuance of precepts by filing a written-objection. The learned District Judge after hearing both the parties rejected the application by his impugned order dated 18.2.2010. Hence, the decree-holder as petitioner was compelled to file the instant revisional application before this Court and obtained the present Rule with an order of injunction.

4. Mr. Ramzan Ali Sikder, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that the learned District Judge, Dhaka committed an error of law in rejecting the decree-holder's application for attachment of the judgment-debtor's property and issuance of precepts holding, inter alia, that admittedly the Court is a transferee Court and it is well settled that a transferee Court is not competent to issue precept. According to Mr. Sikder it was not only erroneous but misconstrued the definition, scope and enforceability of "Award" and "judgment" and "decree" as has been provided in the Arbitration Act-2001, and as such, the impugned order is liable to be set aside. He further submitted that the Court below committed error of law as well as failed to appreciate that the Award of Liverpool Cotton Association was subsequently made Rule of the Court of the Royal Courts of Justice, Admiralty and Commercial Registry, England, which is according to the Arbitration Act, 2001 enforceable in Bangladesh by filing execution case before the learned District Judge, Dhaka assuming as the decree passed by, the District Judge, Dhaka and as such," the learned District Judge committed an error of law in rejecting the application for attachment of the judgment-debtor's property and issuance of the precepts. He further added that view taken by the learned District Judge that precepts only can be issued by the Courts, who passed the decree is not controversial but if the execution case arises out of a foreign Arbitration Award the learned District Judge ought to have considered and read the provisions of Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 together with the Section 46 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submitted that the learned District Judge took erroneous view and committed an error of law in holding that the Court itself was a transferee Court as to the decree in question. Therefore, he rejected the application on a misreading of Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 and as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He further added that the learned District Judge failed to construe the provisions of the Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 in its legal perspective for which he came to a wrong decision and consequently passed the impugned order rejecting the application for attachment and issuance of precepts which is clearly against the spirit of aims and objects of Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001. Mr. Sikder lastly prayed to make the Rule absolute after setting aside the impugned order.

5. None appears to oppose the Rule.

6. Heard the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, perused the revisional application, the impugned order including the materials available in the supplementary affidavits filed in Court.

7. On perusal of the records and the annexures appended to the instant revisional application it reveals that the legal issue before the Court below was whether under Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 the award in question filed before him to be deemed a decree of the Court itself or the transferee Court. On perusal of the impugned order and the opinion formed by the learned District Judge, it appears that the Court itself decided that it is a Court of transferee. From the impugned order it further appears that the Court below opined that a transferee Court cannot issue a precept according to Section 46 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Therefore, the Court below comes to a conclusion that the application filed by the decree-holder is not competent to issue precepts.

8. For the convenience of discussions and to decide the legal issue in question in a execution proceeding which arose out of foreign Award within the ambit of Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001, whether the learned District Judge is a Court of transferee or not and had the authority to issue precepts under such proceedings we feel that it is necessary to quote both the sections 46 of the Code of Civil Procedure and 45 of the Arbitration Act-2001, which runs as follows:

"S. 46.(1) Upon the application of the decree-holder the Court which passed the decree may, whenever it thinks fit, issue a precept to any other Court which would be competent to execute such decree to attach any property belonging to the judgment-debtor and specified in the precept.

(2) The Court to which a precept is sent shall proceed to attach the property in the manner prescribed in regard to the attachment of property in execution of a decree.

Provided that no attachment under a precept shall continue for more than two months unless the period of attachment is extended by an order of the Court which passed the decree or unless before the determination of such attachment the decree has been transferred to the Court by which the attachment has been made and the decree-holder has applied for an order for the sale of such property."

"S. 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 Recognition and enforcement of Foreign arbitral awards-(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, subject to the provisions of section 46-

(a) any foreign award which would be enforceable shall be treated as binding for all purposes on the persons as between whom it was made, and may accordingly be relied on by any of those persons by way of defence, set of or otherwise in any legal proceedings in Bangladesh.

(b) a foreign arbitral award shall, on the application being made to it by any party, be enforced by execution by the Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, in the same manner as if it were a decree of the Court.

(2) ………………………. and  (3) …………………………

Explanation-The expression "Court" shall mean the District Judge's Court exercising the jurisdiction within the district of Dhaka for the purposes of this section."

<u>9. On perusal of Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 it is clear that the intention of the legislature was to extend the Jurisdiction for execution of foreign Award in this territory of Bangladesh.</u>

<u>On a bare reading of Section 45 of the - Arbitration Act, 2001 it appears that the foreign Arbitral award if any submits before the learned District Judge to execute the same as per provision of sub-section (b) of section 45 of the said Act, it will be tantamount to the decree of the Court before  which it is filed.</u>

<u>However, on perusal of the impugned order we find no reasons whatsoever Justifying to dislodge the provision of Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 as has been done in the impugned order refusing to issue the precept.</u>

10. We are of the view that the learned District Judge, Dhaka, who started the execution proceeding to execute a foreign Award is not a Court of transferee, rather, within the purview of Section 45 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 the learned District Judge, Dhaka itself ought to have assumed the Award in question is a decree of his own. However, refusing to accept the foreign Award as the decree of the Court below a clear misconception of law In view of the discussions and reasons made above, we are of the view that the Court below committed an error of law in not allowing the application filed by the decree-holder under Order 21, rule 54(1) read with Sections 46 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

11. Therefore, we find substance in the Rule. Thus, the Rule having merit, it succeeds.

12. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

13. The impugned order dated 18.2.2010 passed by the leaned District Judge, Dhaka in Money Execution Case No. 01 of 2009 is hereby set aside.

14. The application filed under Order XXI, rule 54(1) read with Sections 45 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is hereby allowed.

15. The learned District Judge, Dhaka is directed to take necessary steps in accordance with law and observation as made hereinabove.

16. The office is directed to communicate this judgment at once.

17. Let the order of injunction passed at the time of issuance of the Rule be recalled and vacated.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Latifur Rahman, J : These two petitions by the Second-Party petitioner are directed against the judgment and order passed by the Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 95 of 1989 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree passed by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 184 of 1985making the award the Rule of the court. 

2. The short fact relevant for disposal of these petitions are that a contract wasentered into between the parties for supply and installation of Air Conditioning equipments for BTV Auditorium at Rampura, Dhaka. In the said contract there was an arbitration clause and as per 
the contract the first party respondent raised a dispute vide their letter dated 11.1.84 (Exhibit 27) and claimed settlement by way of arbitration. In Title Suit No.120 of 1984 (renumbered as Title Suit No. 77 of 1989) of the Court of 3rd Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Mr. Shafiq Ahmed, Bar-At-Law was appointed Arbitrator for the First Party and the Government Pleader Mr. Mohammad AliMondal was appointed the Arbitrator of the Second Party. After hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record the joint Arbitrators unanimously passed an award and the same was made Rule of the court. 

3. Mr. Abdul WadudBhuiyan, learned Additional Attorney General appearing for the Second party petitioner submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division acted wrongly in not considering the case of counter claim of the petitioner when the same was specifically raised before the Arbitrators and hence they committed misconduct under Section 30 of the Arbitration Act.

4. At the outset it is to be stated that the submission on fact that the joint arbitrators appointed by the parties did not at all consider the case of counter claim of the petitioner is not correct, as from the award itself it appears that the Arbitrators considered the Second parties' case of counter claim and after due consideration found that the counter claims are concocted, false, fictitious and baseless. Apart from this, it appears that the award was filed in Court on 15.6.88 and notice was served upon the defendant on 4.7.88 and no objection was filed under Section 33 of the Arbitration Act within the time prescribed under Article 158 of the Limitation Act. The objection of the petitioner having been filed beyond the period of limitation the same was rejected as barred by limitation. Thus, the learned Additional Attorney General is not correct in his submission that the counter claim of the petitioner was not considered either by the arbitrators or by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. 

5. These petitioners are dismissed. The petitioners are directed to pay the decreetal amount to the respondent within 15 days from date, as undertaken.

End.

Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J.:- The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Parties No. 1-5 to show cause as to which the impugned judgment and decree 29.04.2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, I' Court, Manikganj in Title Appeal No. 119 of 2005 allowing the appeal reversing those of dated 17.08.2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Gheor, Manikganj in Title Suit No. 42 of 2002 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No, 42 of 2002 in the Court of learned Senior. Assistant Judge, Gheor, Manikganj contending inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to the then Zamindars and during C.S. operation the land was recorded in the name of Zaminder Daraka Nath Chandra. The land being vacant was possessed by the people at large of the locality and after Slate Acquisition and  Tenancy Act, 1950 the land has become 'khash' tinder the government. During S.A. operation it was wrongly recorded in the name of some persons and on the basis of that wrong S.A. record the R.S. khatian being No. 122 was prepared wrongly. The people of the locality from the very beginning do possess the land in dispute. The R.S. and S.A. recorded tenants collusively got their names mutated in Mutation Khatian No. 1/87-88. The names of defendant-respondents in respect of the mutation khatian has been annulled pursuant to a Miscellaneous Case No. 3197 of 1997. The defendants filed a Title Appeal No. 21 of 1997 which was dismissed for default on 12.09.2000. Thereafter, for restoration of the suit a miscellaneous case was preferred which was also rejected but due to denial of plaintiffs title by the defendants the plaintiffs instituted the title suit for declaration of title in respect of the suit land. 

3. The contrary case of the defendants No. I-3 in short is thus that the suit land had been owned and possessed by one Foyezee Box ' alias Foyez Box and others. Thereafter the original owners died leaving their heirs and the defendants are the successive heirs of the original owners. The S.A. and R.S. record has been correctly prepared in their names. The recorded tenants transferred the land in favour of the defendants by registered kabla deeds and delivered possession. The defendants are paying rents to the government on the basis of mutation khatian. The plaintiffs having no right, title, interest and possession filed the suit on false allegation. 

4. The 'ranted trial court dismissed the suit for default during its pendency and thereafter the plaintiffs preferred a Miscellaneous Case being No. 4 of 2000 under Order IX rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the suit vacating the order of dismissal. After rejection of that miscellaneous case the instant Title Suit No. 42 of 2002 has been brought on the basis of same cause of action. The learned Assistant Judge, Gheor, Manikganj on completion of trial dismissed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 17.08.2005. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred a Title Appeal No. 119 of 2005 in the court of learned District Judge, Manikganj, which was transmitted to the I" Court of learned Joint District Judge, Manikganj for hearing and disposal. The learned lower Appellate Court hearing the appeal allowed the same and after setting aside the dismissal decree passed by the trial court decreed the original suit on contest by the impugned judgment and decree dated 29.04.2007. 

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the defendant-respondent-petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay. 

6. Mr. Rokon Uddin Mahmood with Mr. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr. Ashok Kumar Paul with Mr. Scum Reza Chowdhury, the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the opposite punier. 

7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal committed illegality and without reversing the findings of the trial court on maintainability point of the original suit reversed the judgment illegally. The learned Advocate further submits that the trial court rightly after elaborate discussions over the facts and law as to Order IX rule 8 and 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure including the provisions laid down in Order XLIII rule I rightly decided the merit of the case against the plaintiffs on point of maintainability inasmuch as the original suit was not maintainable in the form of declaration under the purview of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It was the observation of the learned trial court that under the proviso of Rule I of Order XLIII of the Code of Civil Procedure in the instant case the original suit was barred by law and on the same cause of action a fresh suit cannot he instituted. On the contrary; the appellate court below illegally held that there is no legal bar in institution of the fresh suit on the same cause of action as it does not attract the provisions laid down in Order XLIII, Rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverter the argument advanced from the side of the petitioners and submits that the appellate court rightly and legally decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the appellant and as the original snit was dismissed for default for the lack of taking step from the side of the plaintiffs and due to the lacking of the party concerned in taking step the suit was dismissed on technical cause there is no scope to invoke the provisions laid down in Order XLIII, Rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate further submits that the earlier suit inasmuch as for want of taking step was dismissed under Order IX rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the learned appellate court below in his observation and findings legally and properly held that the earlier suit being No. 21 of 1997 was filed by the plaintiff-appellants on a cause of action which was occasioned at the fag-end of the month of 'Chaitra', 1403 B.S. and the satiric was dismissed for default on 12.09.2000. Subsequently; the miscellaneous case was preferred for restoration of the same which was also rejected. Therefore; obviously the original suit i.e. the Title Suit No.42 of 2002 was quite maintainable. 

9. Heard the learned Advocates of both sides, panted the case records, exhibited documents, deposition of the witnesses and all other connected papers. 

10. On perusal of the case records in consultation with the submission given from the side of the learned counsel of the parties; the pertinent question which is raised is such as to whether the original suit was maintainable under the purview of law. In this regard; having gone through the relevant case records 1 find that the Title Suit 21 of 1997 was dismissed for default due to the fault of the concerned 'mohorar' on behalf of the plaintiffs. I have come across from the contents of the connected papers that the Title Suit being No.21 of 1997 was fixed for show cause including return of postal summon-notices, but due to lack of taking any step from the side of the plaintiffs the learned court below dismissed the suit for default of the plaintiffs. With regard to this; the provisions laid down in Rule 3 of Order IX of the Code of Civil Procedure contemplates, where neither party appears when the suit is called on for hearing the court may make an order that the suit be dismissed. This type of dismissal order not being a decree is not appealable and the remedy lies on an application under Order IX rule 4 or institution of a fresh suit. There is no scope to entertain Review application here. Secondly, under the proviso laid down in Rule-8 of the said Order IX of the Code of Civil Procedure enjoins, where the defendant appears and the plaintiff does not appear and the suit is called on for hearing the court shall make an order that the suit be dismissed. Here in the instant suit No. 21 of 1997 it is apparent from the face of the papers that there was no occasion for appearance of the defendant after service of summons inasmuch as the service of summon-notices was not done or took its effect or that the process was completed. The date was fixed for taking step from the side of the plaintiffs with regard to postal notices upon the defendants as well as reply of a show cause from the side of the plaintiffs but admittedly no step was taken from the side of the plaintiffs and accordingly the suit was dismissed for default. Under the ambit of Order XLIII Rule I and the proviso laid down in Rule 1(C), an order under rule 9 of Order IX rejecting an application for an order to set aside the dismissal of a suit and fd) an order under Rule 13 of Order IX rejecting an application ( n a case open to appeal) for an order to set aside a decree passed ex parte an appeal shall lie. The learned Advocate Mr. Selim Reza Chowdhury in this connection cited some decisions given in the case of Soneli Bank -vs.- Nurad Kader and another 46 DLR 21, Maung Ahmin -vs.-Maung Sating and another A.I.R.1938 Rangoon 360 and Sheikh Mahammad As: Mt. Rukinina Kunwar and others A.I.R. 1946 Allahabad 506. 

11. Having regard to the cited case laws with the relevant provisions laid down in 
Order XLIII rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1 have every reason. to inclined such a view that Order IX rule 8 has application only to those cases where on the date fixed for hearing of a suit the plaintiff fails to appears. Obviously; it was for taking necessary step from the side of the plaintiff before completion of hearing and in that stage for default the suit was dismissed. Hence; on the same cause of action there is no legal embargo to institute afresh suit under Specific Relief Act. The learned appellate court despite in his observation and findings did not enter into the question of law as spelt out, even then; the decision arrived at by the lower appellate court appears to be fair and legal. More misquoting of section as submitted from the side of the learned counsel for the added opposite parties in filing of the Miscellaneous Case No.4 of 2000 cannot be a legal embargo in getting appropriate relief under law. 

12. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above I am constrained to hold such a view that the Rule have got no merit to succeed. 

13. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 29.04.2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Court, Manikganj in Title Appeal No. 119 of 2005 allowing the appeal and reversing those of dated 17.08.2005 passed. by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Gheor, Manikganj, in Title Suit No. 42 of 2002 is hereby affirmed. 

14. Let a copy of the judgment along with the Lower Court's Record be sent down immediately.

End.

full_judgment:
S.K. Sinha J: Defendant Nos. 1 and 3-8 in a suit for declaration of title are seeking leave to appeal in this Division from a judgment of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2740 of 2002 which has reversed the judgments of the Courts below and decreed the suit.

2. Short facts as disclosed in the plaint arc that the suit schedule Nos. 1-3, measuring an area of 2.72 acres, originally belonged to one Prasanna Kaman Dasi who, transferred the same by a deed dated 14th June, 1919 in favour of Zogendra Lal Das and Mohendra lal Das. They mutated their names in R.S. khatian in equal shares. Mohendra lal Das got 1.36 acres in his share who transferred .80 acre in favour of his wife Josoda Kumari by kabala dated 13th November, 1928. Josoda Kumari while enjoying right, title and possession died leaving the plaintiff as only son to inherit her property. As the plaintiff was staying at different places in connection with his service, he failed to attend during B.S. survey at home. Taking advantage of his absence, the defendants managed to record their names, which clouded his title in the suit land. Mohendra Lal Das transferred to his wife Josoda Kumari, .80 acre keeping only .56 acre, which he transferred in favour of defendant Nos.2-14 by different deeds. Plaintiff and his predecessors did never transfer any property. Principal defendants by practicing fraud managed to record suit land in their names in B.S. Khatian beyond plaintiffs knowledge.

3. Case of the defendant No.1 is that he is the son of Sarin Bala, a sister of Jogendra Lal Das and Mohendra Lal Das. She was married to Zudhistir who died when he was a child. Sarju Bala was brought with him to her paternal house by her brothers and gave her shelter by constructing a house over R.S. Plot No.1821. Subsequently Jogendra transferred his share to his wife Sudha Rani on 14th February, 1953 by way of a gift. Mohendra and Sudha Rani executed deeds dated 14th October, 1956 giving permission to enjoy .0712 acre of land to Sarju Bala and then orally gifted her (Sarju Bala) another .0512 acre of land. After the death of Sarju Bala her son, this defendant No.1 being the only heir has been enjoying .13 acre of the suit land, which land was recorded in B.S. khatian in his name. Mohendra Lal Das filed an objection Case No.476 dated 17th August, 1876 against this recording but it was rejected.

4. Defendant Nos.2-14 also contested the suit denying the claim of the plaintiff. Defendant Nos.15-17, 18-20 and 23 also filed separate written statements and contested the suit denying the claim of the plaintiff in the suit land.

<u>5. The learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit holding that the mother of the plaintiff could not get possession of the suit land on the basis of the deed of 1928. On appeal from the said judgment by the defendants, the Court of appeal below affirmed the judgment of the trial Court observing that the defendant No.1 proved his possession in pursuance of the deed of gift dated 14th November, 1958; exhibit-Ka. that the plaintiff did not challenge the defendants deeds exhibits-A-The executed by Mohendra to Ashiaron Rahman, that the record was also prepared accordingly, that the deed of 1928 in favour of the plaintiffs mother was not acted upon 'and' that the defendants have been able to prove their possession in the suit land, The petitioner thereupon moved the High Court Division a revision petition. A Single Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment decreed the suit and reversed the findings of the Courts below on the reasoning’s that P.Ws.1 and 2 deposed in support of the plaintiffs possession and D.W.4 admitted the possession of the plaintiff, that Mohendra transferred more lands than the Share he was legally entitled to and that the record of right did not extinguish the plaintiff's title unless, the deed of 1928 is set aside.</u>

<u>6. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that the High Court Division exceeded its jurisdiction in exercise of his revisional power in interfering with the concurrent findings of fact arrived at by the Courts below that the deed dated 15th November, 1928 in favour of Josoda, mother of the plaintiff, never acted upon and that the defendants predecessors having purchased the suit land by different deeds from Suds Rani, wife of Gogendra, who is father of the plaintiff and they having been possessed the suit land after purchase, the High Court Division erred in law in reversing the findings arrived at by the Courts below in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction.</u>

<u>7. On perusal of the judgments and other materials on record, we find merit in the contentions of the learned Counsel. Leave is, therefore, granted to consider the additional grounds as under:</u>

<u>"I. Whether the High Court Division committed error of law in setting aside the concurrent findings of the Courts below that the kabala of the plaintiff was not acted upon without properly adverting to the reasons assigned by the Courts below.</u>

<u>II. Whether in the absence of any infirmity in the finding of fact the High Court Division can set aside the concurrent finding of fact of the Courts below."</u>

7. Security of Tk. 1000/- is to be deposited within 1(one) month.

9. Petitioner is permitted to prepare the paper book out of court in accordance with rules.

10. The order of stay granted earlier be extended till disposal of the appeal.

End.
