case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 2nd day of March, 2010 passed by the High Cowl Division in Civil Revision No. 1737 of 1996).
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J: Delay of 163 days in filing the leave petition is condoned.

2. This petition for leave to appeal has been filed by the petitioners against the judgment and order dated the 2nd day of March, 2010 passed by a single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1737 of 1996 discharging the Rule.

3. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 84 of 1991 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Additional Court No. 3, Khulna against the present petitioners and pro-forma respondent Nos. 3 and 4 for declaration that the initiation of V.P. Case No. 9 of 1984(KDA) and issuance of the notice dated 27.09.1984 directing them to surrender possession of the suit land were illegal, void and without jurisdiction and for mandatory injunction to restore back possession of the suit land to the plaintiffs.

4. The plaint case, in short, is that the suit land belonged to Mahmuda Begum and accordingly the same was recorded in the S.A. Khatian in her name. While Mahmuda Begum was in possession of the suit land as the rightful owner, she constructed a 2(two) storied building therein by taking loan from the House Building Finance Corporation in Loan Case No.  KL/6. Mahmuda Begum dug a pond in the suit land and also planted various trees. Mahmuda Begum entered into an agreement with the plaintiffs to sell the suit land along with the pucca structures thereon. Subsequently, Mahmuda Begum sold the suit land to the plaintiffs by executing and registering 3 kabalas on 09.06.1969. The plaintiffs paid up the loan of the House Building Finance Corporation. After purchase the plaintiffs got possession of the suit land and erected boundary wall. The plaintiffs mutated their names and paid rents. The plaintiffs also constructed a room in the 2(two) storied building. The plaintiffs used to exercise died right of possession in the suit land by letting out the same to the Manager, Aqua Marine Limited. On 27.09.1984 suddenly the defendants gave a notice to the plaintiffs to hand over possession of the suit land treating the same as vested and non-resident property. The plaintiffs appeared before the defendants on 07.10.1984 and filed an application for time but the prayer was rejected. Defendant No. 1 was trying to take possession of the suit land by enlisting the same as vested and non-resident property. During the pendency of the suit defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were also trying to recognize the tenants of the plaintiffs as their tenants. The cause of action for the suit arose on 27.09.1984 when defendant No. 1 treated the suit land as vested and non-resident property and asked the plaintiffs to hand over possession thereof to them.

5. The suit was contested by defendant Nos .1 and 3 by filing separate sets of written statement.

6. In the written statement filed by defendant No. 1 it was contended, inter-alia, that that the suit land belonged to Bepin Bihari Datta who transferred the same to Dilip Kumar Roy by way of lease on 13.12.1954 for 20 (twenty) years. Subsequently, Dilip Kumar Roy most illegally gave a power of attorney to one Kawsar Uddin on 17.05.1956 to look after the property. On the basis of the said power of attorney Kawsar Uddin created a deed in favour of his wife on 25.06.1958 though no consideration passed and during S.A. operation the same was wrongly recorded in her name. Bepin Bihari left for India in 1965 and started living there perconsequently the suit property became enemy property and the same vested in the Government. The Government has been enjoying the property through the lessee by treating the same as vested and non-resident property.  The plaintiffs vendor, Mahmuda Begum had no right, title and possession in the suit property. As the plaintiffs filed the suit making false statement, the same was liable to be dismissed with cast.

7. Defendant No. 3 in his written statement contended similar facts as stated by defendant   No. 1 adding further that he has been living in the suit property from 1974. The plaintiffs by claiming ownership of the 1 suit property got a document signed by the defendant admitting him as their tenant. When defendant No. 1 wanted to give lease of the suit property vide V.P. Case No. 9 of 1984 the defendant being in possession of the same for long applied for giving him lease. Accordingly, by a lease deed dated 29.10.1984 the suit property was leased out to the defendant on 29.10.1984 and he has been in possession thereof as lessee.

8. On conclusion of hearing of the suit, the learned Assistant Judge, Additional Court No. 3, Khulna by his judgment and decree dated 12.11.1991 dismissed the suit. Against the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 463 of 1991 before the District Judge, Khulna. The learned Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Khulna who heard the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 27.07.1994 allowed the same and decreed the suit declaring the vested property Case No. 9 of 1984 (KDA) and the notice dated 27.09.1984 issued in the said case upon the plaintiffs directing them to Surrender possession of the suit property as illegal, without jurisdiction and also directing the defendants to deliver possession of the suit property to the plaintiffs within 30 days from the date of decree.

9. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court, the Government-defendants filed Civil Revision No. 1737 of 1996 before the High Court Division. A single Bench of the High Court Division which heard the Civil revision by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule affirming those passed by the appellate Court; hence this petition for leave to appeal.

10. Mr. Bishwa Deb Chakrobarty, learned Deputy Attorney General, appearing for the petitioners, has contended that in view of the fact that notice to surrender possession of the suit property was given to the plaintiffs on 27.09.1984 in VP. Case No. 9 of 1984 (KDA) treating the same vested and non-resident property the plaintiffs' title in the suit property was very much clouded so the suit for declaration simpliciter that initiation of the vested Property case and notice issued therein asking the plaintiffs to surrender possession of the suit property as illegal and without jurisdiction without declaration of title to the suit property was not maintainable under section 42 of the Special Relief Act (the Act), therefore, the appellate Court erred in law in decreeing the suit, and the learned lodge of the High Court Division failed to consider the said legal aspect of the case and thus fell into an error in affirming those of the appellate Court by the impugned judgment and order. The learned Deputy Attorney General has further contended that the trial Court gave clear finding that although the plaintiffs amended the plaint by adding the prayer for mandatory injunction to restore hack possession of the suit property to them on the averments that the tenant (defendant No. 3) accepted "the defendants" as landlord which "tantamounts to dispossession during pendency of the suit.", but they having been evicted from the suit property prior to the, filing of the suit on 03.11.1984, the suit without the prayer for recovery of kilos possession was not maintainable, but the appellate Court though last Court of fact totally failed to consider this finding of the trial Court in reversing its decision and the learned Judge of the High Court Division in a casual manner affirmed the finding of the appellate Court and thus fell into an error in discharging the Rule. The learned Deputy Attorney General has lastly contended that the plaintiffs' vendor, Mahmuda Begum did not acquire any title to the suit property by virtue of her purchase from the attorney of the lessee Dilip Kumar Roy, moreso, the plaintiffs failed to prove their kabalas dated 09.06.1969 as required by the rules of evidence and thus they failed to prove their title to the suit property, Consequently, they were not entitled to get any relief in the suit and as such, the learned Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in affirming the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court and, therefore, interference is called for with the impugned judgment and order by granting leave by this Court.

11. Mr. Quamrul Haque Siddiqui, learned Counsel, entering caveat on behalf of respondent No. 1, on the other hand, has made submissions supporting the judgment passed by the High Court Division.

<u>12. Plaint has not been incorporated in the paper book, but from the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the suit was filed for declaration that the initiation of vested property Case No. 9 of 1984 (KDA) and the notice issued in the said case on 27.09.1984 asking the plaintiffs to hand over possession of the suit property was illegal, without jurisdiction and also for a mandatory injunction to restore back possession of the suit property to the plaintiffs. From the findings of the trial Court it further appears that plaintiff No.  1 as P.W.1 admitted in his cross-examination that the Government took over possession of the suit property from them by force in 1984. The trial Court further found that after taking possession of the suit property the Government leased out the same to defendant No. 3 on 29.10.1984, whereas the suit was filed on 03.11.1984, so the plaintiffs having been dispossessed from the suit property before filing of the suit they were required to pray for recovery of khas possession as per the provisions of section 42 of the Act. In coming to the above findings, the trial Court also noticed that the plaintiffs filed an application for amendment of the plaint on 28.10.1999 adding the prayer for restoration of possession of the suit property by mandatory injunction which was allowed by the Court on 25.11.1999 on averments to the effect</u>

<u>"That tenant has also accepted the defendants as landlord. This tantamounts to dispossession during pendency of the suit."</u>

<u>13. The trial Court further found that the general power of attorney given by Dilip Kumar Roy; a lessee in favour of Kawsar Uddin on 27.07.1956 who transferred the suit property to Mahmuda Begum, vendor of the plaintiffs was not legal and by virtue of such transfer Mahmuda Begum did not acquire any title to the suit property, so also the plaintiffs by their purchase from Mahmuda Begum by the 3(three) kabalas dated 09.06.1969. Moreover, the said kabalas were not proved as per the rules of evidence. With the above findings the trial Court came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs having been dispossessed prior to the filing of the suit their suit without the prayer for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession was not maintainable in law, in view of the provision of section 42 of the Act. From the judgment of the appellate Court it appears that it did not reverse the findings of the trial Court as to the maintainability of the suit and in fact, it decreed the suit mainly on the view that after the repeal of Ordinance No. 1 of 1969 on 23.03.1974 no property could be treated as vested and non-resident properly. It further appears that the appellate Court also found title of the plaintiffs in the suit property on the basis of adverse possession although admittedly from 09.06.1969 till the filing of the suit on 03.11.1984 only 14 years elapsed and title by adverse possession against the Government cannot accrue before expiry of 60 years. From the judgment of the High Court Division it appears that the learned Judge did not at all consider the findings given by the trial Court particularly as to the maintainability of the suit in the light of the provision of section 42 of the Act and in a very casual manner after quoting the findings of the two Courts below affirmed those of the appellate Court.</u>

<u>14. Considering the Findings of the trial Court, the pleading of the plaintiffs as well as the admission of P.W.1 in his cross-examination that the Government took possession of the suit property by force in 1984, we find merits in the submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney General and accordingly, leave is granted to consider the following points:</u>

<u>I. Whether the plaintiffs' suit for declaration simpliciter that the initiation of the V.P. Case No. 9 of 1984 (KDA) and the notice dated 27.09.1984 issued therein asking them to hand over possession of the suit property to the defendants as illegal and without jurisdiction without the prayer for declaration of title to the suit property was maintainable in law within the meaning of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, inasmuch as with the very initiation of the vested property case in question in respect of the suit property and the notice given therein asking the plaintiffs to surrender possession thereof their title to the suit property was very much clouded.</u>

<u>II. Whether the learned Judge of the High Court Division was justified in making the Rule absolute affirming the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court inasmuch as the plaintiffs suit without prayer for recovery of khas possession was not maintainable in law in view of the finding of the trial Court that they were dispossessed from the suit property before filing of the suit.</u>

<u>III. Whether the learned Judge of the High Court Division was correct in affirming the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court finding title of the plaintiffs to the suit property inasmuch as their vendor Mahmuda Begum did not acquire any title in the suit property by virtue of her purchase from Kawsar Uddin the alleged attorney of Dilip Kumar Roy, a lessee of the original owner Bipin Bhihari Datta and further the plaintiffs failed to prove their kabalas dated 09.06.1969 as per the rules of evidence.</u>

15. The petitioners are permitted to prepare the paper book out of Court in accordance with Rules.

16. The operation of the judgment and order dated the 2nd March, 2010 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1737 of 1996 is stayed till disposal of the appeal.

End.

Mr. Sharif Uddin Chaklader, J:- This Rule, at the instance of plaintiff, directed against judgment and decree dated 23.10.2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Monshigonj allowing Title Appeal No.198 of 2000 thereby on arising those dated 21.09.2000 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Munshigonj dismissed Title Suit No.43 of 2000. 

2. Plaintiff instituted the aforesaid suit for recovery of possession on evicting defendants as they are possessing the suit land on permission. 

3. Mr. Md. Asbraful Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner by filling application under Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the pleading submits that advertently plaintiff did not pray for declaration of title and submits that if this amendment be allowed, then in fact the nature and character of the suit will not be changed in any manner. 

4. Mr. Sheikh Md. Sirajul Islam, learned Advocate appearing for the defendant opposite parties denied the submissions of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioners but he did not file any counter affidavit and verbally submits that in revisional jurisdiction this Court has limited jurisdiction by which this Court cannot allow amendment of the pleading and further submits that law required that amendment can be allowed after giving proper opportunity to defendant to deny the statements of amendment by filing written statement and submits that in proper course, the suit should be send back on remand to the trial Court. 

5. Plaintiff's case is that suit land originally belonged to Rajmohan Gope, Lal Mohan Gope, Nepal Chandra Gape and Gopla Chandra Gope in equal shares their names were dully recorded in C.S. Khatian. Thereafter, Rajmohan Gope died leaving 4 sons, Brindabon, Sree Charan, Dalfu and Suklas as heirs. Gopal Chandra Gope died leaving daughter of predeceased son, namely Sudhi Gopini where Jagadish Chandra Poddar, Satish Chandra Poddar Sirish Chandara Poddar and Sot Chandra Poddar obtained money decree in Money Suit No.479 of 1935 against the heirs and tenants of C.S. recorded owners. Thereafter the suit property was sold out in auction through Money Execution Case No.265 of 1936 in favour of Khetra Mohan Gope. Thereafter Khetro Mohan Gope sold the suit property to one Saijuddin by registered deed No.1574 dated 25.08.1948 whose name recorded in S. A. Khatian No.288 Saijuddin gifted the suit property to his wife Rosomonnesa Bibi by way of registered heba deed dated 08.02.1967. Recent R.S record has been prepared in the name of above Rosomonnesa who again sold out .07 acre of land to. Joshna Begum and Mofazzal Hossain by two deeds being Nos.317 and 318 dated 02.07.1977. Rosomonnesa also transferred rest .11 acre of land in favour of her sons and daughter i.e. the plaintiffs through heba-bil-ewaj deeds - who mutated their names vide Mutation Case No.664/1998-1999 and paid rents regularly. Defendant Nos. 1-4 after taking permission from plaintiffs for a period of 4 years, constructed huts on 'KM' schedule of the plaint. They promised to surrender the same when required but defendants Nos. 1-4 denied to surrender the same in favour of plaintiffs, hence the suit. 

6. Defendants Nos.1-4 and the predecessor of opposite parties Nos.5-16 contested the suit by filling written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaint and it is their case that C.S. recorded owner Rajmohan Gope by amicable arrangement amongst his other brothers, got the suit property died leaving 4 sons, Brindabon Sree Charan, Radhika alias Domfu and Suklal Gope as heirs who mortgaged the suit land to the loan office limited Munshigonj who obtained decree in Money Suit No.68 of 1935 and got possession through Execution Case No.20 of 1937. Secretary of loan office purchased the same who allowed Brindabon and others to reside there on compromise. Loan office transferred .04 1/2 acres of land of suit plot along other land to Sree Brindabon Gope, Radhika, Suklal Gope and Khiroda Sundari, wife of Sree Charan Gope by registered deed dated 08.03.1948. Khiroda Sundmi died leaving son, Radheshayam. S.A. record prepared in the name of Brindabon and Radheshayam but wrongly was not recorded in the name of Sukal Gope and. Dompu Gope. Sukal died leaving wife and son Sunil. By an amicable arrangement .04 5'z acre of land of suit plot fell in saham of Dompu, Profulla Bala and Sunil who entered into an arrangement for sale with defendant No.5 on 23.02.1970 and got kabala by decree of Title Suit No.06 of 1971. In this may defendant No.5 became owner and possessor, let out suit property to defendants Nos.1-4. 

7. On the pleadings of the parties trial court decreed the suit, appellate court dismissed the suit. 

8. Since the suit as we see, from the fact as disclosed above sinless the title of the plaintiffs be declared, plaintiffs cannot succeed in the suit for eviction of unauthorized allottee of them, possessor. We have gone through the submissions of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner and of the view that on the pleading of the parties we find suit has been brought against wrong recording not for declaration of title which by amendment of the pleading plaintiffs wanted to implead which in fact did not change the nature and character of the suit as on fact of the given case declaration of title to the suit is required. We find substance in the rule. 

9. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. 

10. The judgments complained are set aside. Title Suit No.43 of 2000 is sent back to the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Munshigonj for disposal of the suit on the light of the observations made in the body of the judgment within 1(one) year from the date of receiver of the judgment after giving chance to the plaintiff to amend the pleadings and also allow the defendants to contest the amendment of the pleadings. 

11. Send down the lower court records. 

12. Communicate this order at once. 

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Md. Idrisur Rahman with Mr. Md. Shahidullah and Mr. Md. Bodiuzzaman Tapadar, Advocates ------ For the petitioners 
Mr. Mohammad Ali, Advocate ------ For the respondent
parties:
Arun Kumar Sutradhar and another ------ Petitioners
Vs
The Joint District Judge, Artha Rin Adalat Comilla and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Quddus, J.: This Rule Nisi, at the instance of two judgment debtors in a mortgage decree, was issued calling in question order dated 26.5.2003 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Comilla in Artha Decree Execution Case No. 44 of 1995 (arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 182 of 1992) issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioners to put them in civil prison.

2. The petitioners' case in short is that respondent No. 2, Sonali Bank Ltd. as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No.182 of 1992 in the Artha Rin Adalat, Comilla against the petitioners and others for recovery of loan amounting to Tk.6,39,608.55 (taka six lac thirty nine thousand six hundred eight take and paisa fifty five) only by selling the mortgaged property and the said suit was decreed on contest against petitioner No: 1 and ex-parte against others by judgment and decree dated 31.5.1994. Thereafter, the decree-holder bank on obtaining the final decree, put the same in execution by, filing Artha Decree Execution Case No. 44 of 1995. The executing Court after observing the necessary formalities fixed 15.3.1998 for holding auction sale of the mortgaged property. At this stage one Abdul Latif and some others filed Miscellaneous Case No.3 of 1998 under Order XXI rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure for releasing the attached property before the executing Court and obtained an order staying the execution proceedings till disposal of the Miscellaneous Case. The decree-holder bank contested the said Miscellaneous Case by filing a written objection. Ultimately the learned Judge of the executing Court heard the Miscellaneous Case and allowed the same in pint by his judgment and order dated 24.1.2001 releasing a portion of the attached property (vide annexe:B-1 to the writ petition). The decree-holder bank after taking several adjournments, filed an application for amendment of the execution case on 25.7.2002, which the executing Court allowed on 6.5.2003.

3. In the above background the decree-holder bank filed an application on 26.5.2003 praying for warrant of arrest against judgment debtors No.1 and 3 (herein the petitioners) to put them in civil prison, which the executing Court allowed and issued warrant of arrest against them by order dated 26.5.2003 and fixed 14.6.2003 for compliance and return of the warrant. Being aggrieved by the said order, the petitioners moved the present writ petition, obtained the Rule and order staying operation of the impugned order.

4. The decree-holder bank as respondent No.2 contests the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia, that the petitioners had fraudulently sold out a' portion of the mortgaged property to others before taking loan from the bank and by concealing the said fact caused huge loss to the bank, but the executing Court without considering these facts had allowed the Miscellaneous Case releasing .98 3/4 acres of land, a portion of the mortgaged property. The respondent's further case is that the executing Court attempted to sell the mortgaged property by fixing a date for holding auction on 15.3.1998, but no bidder participated. After disposal of the Miscellaneous Case, the decree-holder bank filed an application on 26.5.2003 for issuing warrant of arrest against the judgment-debtors (herein the petitioners) and the executing Court rightly issued the warrant of arrest to put them in civil prison so that they are compelled for payment of the decretal amount.

5. Mr. Md. Idrisur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the impugned order apparently shows that the executing Court had allowed the application for substitution of one of the judgment debtors, but issued warrant of arrest against all to put them in civil prison in violation of section 34 (2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain,2003 (in brief 'the Ain'). The learned Advocate further submits that after the schedule of the execution case was amended on 6.5.2003 releasing a portion of the mortgaged property, no further step was taken by the decree-holder bank for selling the remaining portion and therefore, the provision of section 34 (9) of the Ain was not complied with and without such compliance, issuance of warrant of arrest was in clear violation of law and therefore without lawful authority.

6. On the other hand, Mr. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate for respondent No.2 submits that as the decree-holder bank attempted to sell the mortgaged property by fixing a date for auction on 15.3.1998, the provision of section 34 (9) of the Ain was thus complied with and no further compliance was necessary. The executing Court rightly issued the warrant of arrest against the judgment debtors under section 34 (10) of the Ain, and as such the rule is liable to be discharged.

7. We have perused the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition and papers submitted therewith, and considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides. We have also examined the legal position and the relevant laws. It appears from the mortgage decree (annexe: A-1 to the writ petition) that the name of petitioner No.1, Arun Kumar Sutradhar is figured as defendant No.1 in the capacity of Proprietor, M/S Smrity Tin Industries. The name of his father, Satish Chandra Sutradhar also appears as defendant No.2 and that of writ petitioner No.2 Dhrubaraj Brahmma as defendant No.3. On the death of defendant No. 2, Satish Chandra Sutradhar, the name of petitioner No.1 was substituted at the instance of the decree holder bank, though it was not necessary as his (petitioner-1's) name was already on record as defendant No.1. Since the name of petitioner No.1 was on record from the very inception of the suit as a principal defendant, the submission advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioners in respect of section 34 (2) of the Ain has no leg to stand.

<u>8. In order to appreciate the second limb of his argument, we have examined the order sheets of the Artha Decree Execution Case. It appears that an attempt to sell the mortgaged property was made before disposal of the Miscellaneous Case under Order XXI rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But after allowing the Miscellaneous Case and amendment of the schedule of the Execution Case, no subsequent step whatsoever was taken to sell the remaining portion of the mortgaged property. Under the circumstances, we hold that the decree holder bank was required to take step afresh for selling the mortgaged properly after amendment of the schedule of the execution case, failing which, it cannot be said that section 34(9) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was complied with. It is the cardinal principle of interpretation of statute that any provision of law, which takes away the man's freedom, should be construed strictly.</u>

In view of the above, we find substance in the Rule. As a result, the Rule is made absolute and the impugned order dated 26.5.2003 passed by the Aratha Rin Adalat, Comilla in Artha Decree Execution Case No. 44 of 1995 (arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 182 of 1992) issuing warrant of arrest to put the writ petitioners in civil prison is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of or legal effect.

9. The executing Court will, however, be at liberty to issue warrant of arrest afresh against the judgment debtors only after due compliance of section 34(9) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 by selling or attempting to sell the mortgaged property (as described in the amended schedule of the execution case), if it is required.

10. The office is directed to communicate the judgment to the concerned executing Court at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. Khijir Ahmed, Advocate ------ For the petitioner

Mr. Md. Aminul Islam, Advocate ------ For the opposite party No.3

Anarul Islam ------ Defendant-Petitioner
Versus
Government of Bangladesh and Others ------ Plaintiff-Opposite parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal, J:  In this Revisional application under Section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the petitioner calls in question the legality and propriety of the impugned judgment and order dated 03.5.2010 passed by the learned District Judge, Meherpur in Civil Revision No.05 of 2008 remanding the suit to the trial Court after setting aside the order dated 22.5.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Meherpur in Title suit No.05 of 1999 rejecting the plaint. 

2. Facts necessary for the purpose of disposal of this case are as follows:-

The opposite party No.1, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Meherpur as plaintiff instituted a suit being Title Suit No.05 of 1999 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Meherpur for declaration of title on the averments that the suit land along with other lands were vested in favour of the Government though during S.A. operation the record was wrongly prepared in the name of the defendant No. 1 and thereupon, the defendant claimed the suit land and hence the suit. 

3. The defendant petitioner entered appearance in the suit and filed an application under Order 7, Rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint stating, inter alia, that over the selfsame suit land and in between same parties the defendant-petitioner earlier got decree in Title Suit No.448 of 1975 and the said decree was upheld by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4573 of 1995, vide judgment and order dated 18.02.2002 and as such the suit is clearly barred by law of res-judicata.

4. On Revision, the learned District Judge, Meherpur upon hearing the parties by the impugned judgment and order dated 03.5.2010 allowed the Revision and set aside the order dated 22.5.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Meherpur in Title Suit No.05 of 1999 holding that the property as described in the plaint of earlier Title Suit No.448 of 1975 and in the plaint of the present suit are not same and similar and thus, the trial Judge wrongly decided the question of maintainability of the suit without taking evidence. 

5. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order dated 03.05.2010, the present defendant-petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

6. Mr. Khijir Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner after placing the impugned judgment and order submits that the Court of appeal below committed illegality in entertaining the Revisional application against the order of rejection of plaint inasmuch as order of rejection of plaint is appealable and as such the impugned judgment and order is not tenable in law. He next upon referring to the schedule of both the suits submits that dag of the suit property, parties in both the suits are same and it is apparent from the record that the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 after being unsuccessful up to the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4573 of 1995 preferred the instant suit being Title Suit No.05 of 1999 and the learned Joint District Judge was perfectly justified in allowing the petitioner's application under Order 7, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the clear finding that suit is barred by law of res-judicata. He further submits that the lower Revisional Court without applying its judicial mind into the facts and circumstance of the case and law bearing on the subject mechanically arrived at a finding that without taking evidence it is not possible to decide whether the suit is barred by principle of res-judicata and the same has resulted in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. 

7. Mr. Arobinda Kumar Roy, learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the opposite party No.1, on the other hand, supports the impugned judgment and contends that the learned District Judge was perfectly justified in holding that in the facts and circumstances of the case, the plea of res-judicata cannot be decided without taking evidence at the time of trial. 

8. Mr. Md. Aminul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.3 at the very outset adopting the submission of the learned Assistant Attorney General opposes the Rule. 

9. I have heard the learned Advocate and the learned Assistant Attorney General and perused the Revisional application, supplementary affidavit dated 12.11.2012 and other materials on record including the -judgments of two Courts below. The main point for consideration is, already noticed, whether the learned District Judge was right in holding that the learned trial Judge wrongly decided the question of maintainability of the suit without taking evidence in an application under Order 7, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

10. Ongoing through the materials on record, it appears that admittedly the Government, opposite party No.1 after being unsuccessful in Title Suit No.448 of 1975 up • to the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4573 of 1995 filed Title Suit No.05 of 1999 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Meherpur for declaration of title over the self-same suit property. It is also found that contends of both the plaints are almost similar, dag of the suit land of both the suits and parties are same. 

11. On perusal of the order of the trial Court, it appears that the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Meherpur arrived at a finding inter-alia, that: উক্ত মঞ্জুর আদেশ এর বিরুদ্ধে মাননীয় হাইকোর্ট বিভাগের ৪৫৭৩/৯৫ নং সিভিল রিভশন মোকদ্দমা দায়ের হয়। উক্ত সিভিল রিভিশন মোকদ্দমাটি শুনানী অন্তে মাননীয় জেলা আদালতে মিস আপীল ১২/৯৪ কেসটির মঞ্জুর আদেশ বাতিল করেন এবং বিজ্ঞ মুনসেফ আদলতের মিস ১২০/৭৭ নং কেসের আদেশটি বহাল রাখে। সুতরাং দাখিলী কাগজাদি পরযালোচনায় প্রতয়মান হয় নালিশী সম্পত্তির স্বত্ত্ব প্রচারের ডিক্রী এই মোকদ্দমার ১নং বিবাদী বরার অদ্যবধি বহাল আছে। মাননীয় হাইকোর্ট বিভাগের আাদেশের বিরুদ্ধে মাননীয় আপীল বিভাগে কোন প্রতিকার প্রার্থী হয়েছে কিনা, সেটি জানা যায় নাই। অর্থাত একই পক্ষদের মদ্যে একই নালিশী সম্পত্তি নিয়ে, একই প্রার্থনায় আনীত একাধিক মোকদ্দমা অবশ্যই চলতে পারে না। সেক্ষেত্রে এই মোকদ্দমাটি রেসজুডিকেটা দোষে বারিত বটে। সংগত কারণে এই মোকদ্দমাটি রক্ষণীয় নয়। 

These are the findings of fact based on proper and correct appreciation of both law and fact. I find nothing wrong in the trial Court's finding. The Revisional Court below, however, in its turn without adverting the material findings of the trial Court below reversed the decision of the Joint District Judge, Meherpur. So, I am unable to agree with the finding of the lower Revisional Court that the trial Court below wrongly decided the question of maintainability of the suit without taking evidence in an application under Order 7, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

12. The suit is barred by res-judicata, which is a question of fact and law, normally in such type suits plaint cannot be rejected but in this case it is clearly found that over the selfsame suit land and in between same parties the defendant-petitioner earlier got decree in Title Suit No.448 of 1975 and the said decree was upheld by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4573 of 1995 vide judgment and order dated 18.02.2002 and under such facts and circumstances the trial Court below committed no wrong in holding that the suit is clearly barred by principle of res-judicata. The ultimate result of the suit is as clear as day light, the plaintiff should not be allowed to reopen the same matter afresh after losing up to the High Court Division. 

13. Furthermore, the Revisional Court below appears to have committed illegality in entertaining the Revisional application under Section 115(2) CPC against the order of rejection of plaint inasmuch as order of rejection of plaint is appealable. My view is, therefore, that the judgment of the Revisional Court below is not based on proper and correct appreciation of both law and fact. 

14. For the reasons stated above the judgment of the Revisional Court below does not deserve to be sustained. 

15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and order dated 03.5.2010 passed by the learned District Judge, Meherpur in Civil Revision No.05 of 2008 is set aside. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. 

16. Let a copy of the judgment along with the lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.1623 of 2008.
lawyer:
For the Petitioners: Mr. Abu Siddique, Advocate-on-Record. 
Respondents: Not represented.
parties:
Kulsum Vanu Bibi and another ------ Petitioners
Versus
Abdul Jobbar Bhuiyan and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman, J:- Instant leave petition under Article 103 of the Constitution is for granting leave to appeal against the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.I490 of 2006 making the Rule absolute. 

2. In the Civil Revision No.1490 of 2006 the judgment and decree dated 31.01.2006 passed in Title Appeal No.07 of 2005 by the District Judge, Brahmanbaria, allowing the appeal has been challenged. in allowing the appeal the judgment and decree dated 16.10.2004 passed in Title Suit No.28 of 2004 by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Kashba, Brahmanbaria, dismissing the suit, has been set aside and thereby the suit for declaration of title has been decreed. 
3. The plaintiff-appellant hereof filed the 'Title, Suit No.28 of 2004 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Kashba, Brahmanbaria, praying for a decree for simple declaration of title in the suit land. 

4. The trial court on consideration of the materials and evidence on record dismissed the suit holding, amongst others, that the plaintiff No.2 by filing a compromise petition relinquished his claim on the suit land admitting the right, title and interest and possession of the defendant thereon and that possession of the defendant in the suit land has' been admitted by the P.W. Nos.2 and 3 as evidenced from their respective depositions and thus the suit is barred under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act for want of proper prayer for consequential relief in the suit. On appeal, in Title Appeal No.7 of 2005, the plaintiff got the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court set aside and the suit decreed. The appellate Court, as it appears that, although found the possession of the defendant-respondent in the suit land but held the same as permissive possession and without considering the fact of compromise petition filed by the plaintiff No.2 who admitted the right, title and interest and possession of the defendant in the suit land, decreed the suit illegally relying on a decree passed in Title Suit No.78 of 1988. 

5. Being aggrieved the defendant-respondent moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1490 of 2006 and the High Court Division on detailed discussions on the materials on record and the provisions of Order XLI Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure set aside the decree passed by the appellate Court below and thereby the rule was made absolute, observing, amongst others, that:-

"On a meticulous examination of the evidence on record, exhibits, registered deed, documents and also the judgment of both the courts below it appears that the trial Court discussed the evidence and also perused the documents and legal aspect of the case and made his observation that the suit was hit by Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The learned trial Court further held in his judgment that since P.Ws.2 and 3 admitted the possession of the defendant in the suit land the plaintiff ought to have been sought for recovery of khas possession as consequential relief. But the plaintiff instituted a simple suit for declaration of title which is not maintainable and hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The learned District Judge, Brahmanbaria while reversing the judgment of the trial Court did not write a single word about this specific finding of the law point by the trial Court which appears to be manifestly perverse. Moreover, when the plaintiff No.2 during the pendency of the suit in the trial Court by submitting a compromise petition relinquished his claim over 20 decimals of the suit land then the plaintiff Nos. l and 3 ought to have been amended the schedule of the suit land but the plaintiffs did not do so. The observation made by the trial Court was absolutely correct but the lower appellate Court did not at all consider this vital and material point and did not mention anything in his judgment on this point. The lower appellate Court while reversing the judgment of the trial Court is required to reverse the material finding of the trial Court with reference to the evidence on record but the learned District Judge, Brahmanbaria did not do so. The lower appellate Court should assign cogent and reasonable ground in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court. In this connection I like to rely on the decision in the case of Ranjit Sarker and others Vs. Sree Sukhendu Bikahs Biswas and others reported in 17 BLD(AD)58 wherein it has been held: 

Order XLI Rule 31 

Judgment of Reversal. 

The appellate Court failed to advert to the specific reasoning’s of the trial Court nor did it discuss all the material evidence taken into consideration by the trial Court. The gross omission made by the appellate Court is in respect of the clear findings by the trial Court about the deed of agreement for reconveyance and the subsequent deeds of sale as genuine. This goes to the root of the merit of the case. Since no relief could be granted-to the plaintiffs without coming to any finding that any of the said deeds other than the deeds of sale under pre-emption were sham  transaction, the appellate Court was wrong in reversing the judgment of the trial Court in a casual manner.

The impugned judgment of the trial Court it transpires that in arriving in its finding the said Court carefully considered the material evidence and facts and circumstances of the case and also the legal aspect with regard to the maintainability in arriving at its finding because the plaintiff could not prove the possession in the suit land by adducing oral evidence. The lower appellate Court committed an error of law and come to a wrong finding occasioning failure of justice in not considering the possession of the defendant over the suit land which was the materials fact of the case affecting the merit of the case and as such committed error of law which is liable to be interfered by this Court. In this connection I like to refer the case of Hussain Ahmed Chowdhury alias Ahmed Hussain Chowdhury and others Vs. Nurul Amin and others reported in 47 DLR (AD) 162 wherein it has been held. 

'If there is misreading of evidence and non-consideration of some material evidence then it was incumbent on the revisional Court to consider the same and to arrive at a proper finding on the material evidence on record and to finally dispose of the case.' 

In view of the facts and legal position of the case I find that the lower appellate Court is absolutely wrong in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court as such the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court is liable to be set aside."

 6. We have considered the leave petition as well as the judgment passed by the courts below as well as the impugned judgment and order. It appears that the High Court Division on detailed discussion on the judgments passed by the trial Court and the appellate Court below and having found that both the Courts below noticed that the defendants were in possession of the suit land as disclosed by the P.Ws.2 and 3 in their respective depositions as well as by the plaintiff No.2 in its compromise petition filed in the trial Court made the Rule absolute. 

7. The High. Court Division correctly found that the appellate Court erred in not holding that the suit as framed and filed with a prayer for simple declaration is not maintainable in view of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act since the defendants were found in possession. It further appears from the judgments of the Courts below as well as from the impugned judgment passed by the High Court Division that it is the admitted position that the plaintiffs were not in exclusive possession of the suit land and that the plaintiff No.2 filed a compromise petition relinquishing his portion of claim in the suit in favour of the defendant admitting the defendant's right, title and interest and possession thereon. 
In the premises we do not find any merit in the leave petition. 

8. Accordingly, the petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Nuruzzaman, J:- The instant Rule has been obtained by the petitioners calling upon the opposite party Nos. l and 10 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 24.2.1983 and 01.3.1983 respectively passed by the learned District Judge, Khulna in Title Appeal No.06 of 1980 affirming the judgment and decree dated 22.6.1979 and 29.6.1979 respectively passed by the Munsif, 1st  Court, Khulna in Title Suit No.801 of 1976 should not be set aside. 

2. The material facts relevant for disposal of the Rule is that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.801 of 1976 in the Court of the learned Munsif, 1st  Court, Khunla for declaration of title and for permanent injunction. In the prayer portion of the suit the plaintiffs sought for following reliefs: 
"(a) That it be declared that the action of the defdt No.1 issuing D.C.R. in favour of Defdt. 10. The points for consideration are whether the plaintiffs were able, to prove their right and title over the suit property by adducing evidence and the Courts below committed any error of law in passing the judgment and decree. 

11. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits a supplementary affidavit in support of the petitioner's case appending some annexures which are annexures E, F, G, H and I-series. 

12. On considering the conflicting submissions of the learned Advocates for the respective parties, it is pertinent to discuss the evidence to decide the legal issues whether both the Courts below considered the evidence on record in its true and legal perspective. 

13. Now I shall examine whether the Courts below considered the evidence of the plaintiffs' side as to whether they were able to prove their case by adducing oral and documentary evidence. 

14. On consideration of the evidence and materials on record it appears that the plaintiffs adduced as many as 3 witnesses in support of their case. 
P.W.I Satish Chandra Roy deposed in favour of the plaintiffs. In his deposition he stated that Surendra Nath Sardar on 09.10.1963 executed the "will" in favour of the plaintiff Nos.01-04. Bharat Chandra Sardar was the executor of the "will". Bharat as executor after the death of Surendhra filed Miscellaneous Case No.228 of 1967 for probate of the "will". On 04.11.1967 the "will" was made probate and the Court ordered letter of administration. One Dijendra filed a case against the probate which was ended by compromise. The plaintiffs on the strength of the probate were in peaceful possession of the property. After obtaining the probate and letter of administration the plaintiffs filed Miscellaneous Case No.71 of 1970-71 and mutated their names in the record. Thereafter they went to the Tahsil Office for payment of rent wherein they came to know that the suit property was enlisted as enemy property. On 30.11.1976 the defendants No.2-9 threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess from the suit land and they disclosed that defendant Nos.02-5 took lease through DCR, hence, they filed the suit against the defendants for declaration of title and for permanent injunction. He filed the order of probate before the trial Court which was marked as Ext. l. He also submitted the other documents which were exhibited. In cross-examination the defence has failed to find out any material contradiction to the plaintiffs' case. However, the P.W.1 did not make any contradictory statement or contradict any of the points which he has stated in his deposition. 

P.W.2 Bishnupada Dhali, in his deposition stated that he knew the plaintiffs. They have been possessing the suit land. Defendant Dhirendra Nath Sardar also possessed the suit land. They are possessing the same from 1370 B.S. I know the suit land, there is a canal on the south of the suit land and thereafter his land is situated. The Tahsilder of the Government never possessed the suit land; it is not a fact that the defendant Nos.2-9 possessed the suit land. It is not a fact that the DCR holders of the Government possessed the suit land. The plaintiffs never migrated to India and their father also never migrated to India. He knew Surendra Nath Sardar who died in India. It is not a fact that Surendra Nath Sardar left Bangladesh and died in India. Surendra Nath Sardar died in Bangladesh during the period of Pakistan. This is the evidence of P.W.2 from which it appears that he supported the plaintiffs' case not the defence case. Although there is a sentence that Surendra died in India, but thereafter he denied that Surendra Nath Sardar left Bangladesh. He also affirmed that Surendra died in this country during Pakistan period. In cross-examination he also supported his deposition. The defence was not able to make any third case or to contradict any point in their favour. 

P.W.3 Profulla Kumar Sardar in his deposition stated that he knew the plaintiffs' and suit land. He has land contiguous to the suit land. The plaintiffs possessed the suit land. The defendant Dhirendra Nath also possessed the suit land with the plaintiffs. The local Tahsilder never possessed the suit land. He did not see the defendants 02-9 to possess the suit land. The defendant Nos.2-9 and any other DCR holders never possessed the suit land. The plaintiffs never migrated to India. In cross-examination he rightly answered the query of defence as stated in his deposition. He admitted that some of the defendants, namely, Yusuf and Yunus Sheikh possessed the suit land. He denied the suggestion that he deposed before the trial Court falsely in favour of the plaintiffs or he has been gained over by the plaintiffs or they are belonged to the same party. 

15. D.W.1 Dhirendra Lal Sardar in his deposition stated that he is the added defendant in the suit. The plaintiffs sold 16.66 acres of land to him in the year 1963 by a registered deed. On the basis of the solenama he compromised with the plaintiffs and left 4 bighas of land in favour of the plaintiffs. In cross-examination he admitted that Surendra Nath Sardar is his uncle. He and his brother got 97 bighas of land from his father. In his portion he got 481/2 Bighas of land. He submitted the statement with all the properties. In reply of cross-examination he stated that plaintiffs have the right, title and possession over the suit land. He correctly said that Bharat Chandra Sardar was the executor of the "will". He stated that he did not know how many lands possessed by Surendra Nath Sardar. He denied the suggestion that Surendra Nath Sardar migrated to India. He also denied the suggestion that they created the "will". He also denied the suggestion that he created suff-kabala deed without any consideration.  
16. On scrutiny of the evidence on record it reveals that the plaintiffs in support of their case adduced oral and documentary evidence. However, on perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that both the Courts below did not discuss the evidence of the plaintiffs in their respective judgments in its legal perspective. However, they opined that there is no cogent evidence on record to show that Surendra, Nath Sardar had any other property beside the suit land. They also opined that the certified copy of S.A. Khatian Ext.1-series show that even the homestead of Surendra Nath Sardar included in the probate case. It is not natural that Surendra Nath Sardar executed the "will" in respect of the suit property Ir. including his homestead depriving his wife and son from his property. The relationship between the plaintiffs and Surendra Nath Sardar and the relationship between the plaintiffs and executor Bharat Chandra Sardar has not been disclosed in the plaint. Surendra Nath Sardar died at Golapdaha under the P.S. Dumuria, District Khulna on 8th Chaitra, 1373 B.S. But P.W.2 Bishnupada Dhali in his examination-in-chief stated that Surendra Nath Sardar died in India. Form the above discussions of the Courts below, it appears that except one sentence of P.W.2 Bishnupada Dhali quoted in the judgment of both the Courts below others are mere imagination and after thought speculation. However, other evidence which are on record not discussed by both the Courts below. It appears from the discussions of the evidence that the plaintiffs adduced the evidence to prove their right, title and interest over the suit land but both the Courts below opined that they did not disclose the-x relationship with Surendra Nath Sardar. In this point I am of the view that it is not the case of revocation to prove the relationship of legatees and testator and genuineness of the "will". The defendants even did not deny the plaintiff case and proved the enlistment of enemy property by adducing any oral or documentary evidence. Even they did not produce any scrap of papers before the trial Court in favour of their claim showing that the suit land was declared and enlisted as enemy property in due process of law. However, the plaintiffs as petitioners by filing a supplementary affidavit before this Court submits the Annexure-E, which is the certified copy of order dated 4.11.1969 passed by District delegate Subordinate Judge, Khulna and some original deeds, i.e., Annexure-F series and they also produced the certified copy of the annexure-A original "will" with the revisional application which was obtained from the Court of District Judge, Khulna. On perusal of the said documents it appears that the "will" itself speaks about the relationship of Surendra Nath Sardar with legatees and it is the self explanatory "will" from which it is crystal clear that there is a good relationship between the legatees and Surendra Nath Sardar. So, both the Courts below without considering the recital and above legal aspects of the "will" as well as the order of probate and letter of administration passed in Miscellaneous case dismissed the suit which tainted by misreading and misconstruing the evidence on record. Had the learned Judges of the Courts below paid title more attention with their judicial mind to the above oral and documentary evidence they would have seen some thing more for which the decisions of the Courts below would have found affirmative. More-so, from the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the defendants in their written statement did not inscribe any thing on what date and on what basis they claimed the suit land as enemy property nor they submitted the sensor list or an iota of documentary evidence that the suit land is the enemy property. Even the defendants did not examined the alleged lessees nor produced any lease agreements, DCR and any supporting papers to establish that the suit properties were declared as enemy property in due course of law and possessed by the Government. From the defence case, it appears that in written statement they disclosed the number of lease case which was for the year 67-68, on the contrary they issued D.C.R for the year 1976. Although defence did not produce any of the records of lease eases and D.C.R but we astonishingly observe that both the Courts below have failed to notice this vital aspect of the case. 

17. In this regard we may rely to the precedent of apex court to the case of Aroti Rani Paul Vs. Sudarshan Kumar Paul and others, reported in 56 DLR (AD) 73, wherein it was held 
"that since the law of enemy property itself died with the repeal of Ordinance No.1 of 1969 on 23.3.1974 no further Vested Property case can be started thereafter on the basis of the law which is already dead." 
Here, the case in hand the defendants although in written statement mentioned the number of lease case for the year 67-68 which obviously proved that it is beyond approval of the law as it was written before the promulgation of enemy property Ordinance. On the other hand issued the D.C.R. for the year 1976 which clearly indicated that D.C.R. was issued after the repealed of the said Ordinance. Therefore, it is clearly presumed that the defendants for their such activities neither examined any witness nor produced any such documents, if examined and produced such oral and documentary evidence those not helped them but surely depicted and supported the plaintiffs case. 

18. We can refer another precedent to the case of Bangladesh Vs. Md. Aslam and others, reported in 44 DLR (HCD) 69 referring the Sections 101 and 103 of the Evidence Act, wherein it was held that 
"Mere filing of a rent receipt or a private document without formal proof thereof and without proving the contents of such documents cannot fulfill the requirements of law." 

19. In the present case though the defendants claimed that they have started the Miscellaneous Case in the year 1967-1968, however, they did not produce any case record before the trial Court nor in the appellate Court below, even not, in this Court and without filing any documentary evidence the claim of the Vested and Non Resident Property seems to me is nothing but a mere statement in the written statement which can not be treated if so facto as evidence unless or until it was proved in accordance with law before the competent Court.

In the present case from the evidence on records it appears that "will" was executed on 9.10.1963 by Surendara Nath Sarder, by dint of "will" the executor of the will obtained the probate and letter of administration on 4.11.1967 from the competent Court, Thereafter one Dejendra legal heirs of Surendra filed case for canceling the probate which was also compromised and solenama was filed in Court which was accepted by the Court and till day all these Court orders neither challenged by the heirs of the testator nor by the authority of custodian of enemy property. In the mean time plaintiffs sold some lands to the third party who was added in the present suit as added defendant. In order to protect his property he was examined as D.W1. He also mutated his name and paid rent.The added defendant produced all the documents and materials as exhibits. On the above documentary evidence it appears that before promulgation of the enemy property Ordinance the right, title and possession of the Surendara was extinguished in the year 1963 and 1967 and the plaintiffs and added defendant by dinty of legal and valid documents acquired the right, title and possession over the suit land. In such view of matter I do not find any reason to disbelieved oral evidence of P.Ws. regarding the possession of the plaintiff. 

20. For the reasons and discussions made herein above. 
I am of the view that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their case in respect of their title, and as such, entitled for declaration that DCR issued by the defendants is without lawful authority, illegal, mala fide,k void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The property as described in the schedule of the plaint is not enemy or vested and Non-resident Property. 

21. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree of the Courts below are hereby set aside. The suit be decreed in terms of prayer (a) of the plaint. 

22. The prayer for stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.
